items.title: Appointments to Museum Advisory Committee announced
items.description: The Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau announced today (October 20) appointments to the Museum Advisory Committee (MAC) and its three standing sub-committees, namely the Art Sub-committee (ASC), the History Sub-committee (HSC) and the Science Sub-committee (SSC), with the appointment of Professor Douglas So Cheung-tak as Chairperson of the MAC, Professor Desmond Hui Cheuk-kuen as Chairperson of the ASC, Professor Joshua Mok Ka-ho as Chairperson of the HSC and Professor Alexander Wai Ping-kong as Chairperson of the SSC. All appointments are for a two-year term up to October 19, 2028. The MAC and its three standing sub-committees, established on October 20, 2016, comprise members of different backgrounds with a great wealth of professional expertise and experience relevant to the work of museums, including professionals, academics, museum experts, collectors, art promoters, entrepreneurs, marketing and public relations experts, and community leaders. The MAC and its three standing sub-committees advise the Leisure and Cultural Services Department (LCSD) on strategies for development, promotion and management of the public museums. A spokesman for the Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau thanked all the Chairpersons and members of the MAC and its standing sub-committees for their ardent support and invaluable contributions in the past years, including one outgoing MAC member (Dr Ng Tsz-yan), and four outgoing co-opted members (Professor Edwin Chan Ho-yin, Ms Sabrina Leung Heung-ying, Professor Tam Ka-chai and Professor Raymond Tong Kai-yu), and looked forward to receiving the valuable advice of the new MAC and its standing sub-committees on the development of the public museums. The membership list and terms of reference of the MAC are as follows: Chairperson Professor Douglas So Cheung-tak Members Professor Karen Chan Ka-yin Mr Michael Chan Sze-wah Ms Rowena Cheung Po-man Ms Amanda Cheung Zee-yin Mr Chiu Tsang-hei Mr Stanley Choi Tak-shing Professor Apple Chui Pui-yi* Dr Crystal Fok Lo-ming Ms Elizabeth Fung Hoi-yung Mr Andy Hei Kao-chiang Professor Desmond Hui Cheuk-kuen Mr Christopher Kwok Kai-wang Mr Edmund Lai Man-kit Ms Tendy Lam Pui-tung Mr Lam Shu-kam Ms Josephine Lee Yuk-chi Dr James Li Tsz-shu Mr Warren Luk Hua Ms Erica Ma Yun Professor Joshua Mok Ka-ho Ms Joyce Ng Sheung-ching Dr Provides Ng Tsing-yin Dr Chloe Suen Yin-wah Mr James Tong Wai-pong Professor Alexander Wai Ping-kong Dr Jimmy Wong Kam-yiu Ms Anna Yau Wai-yu Official members Principal Assistant Secretary (Culture)2, Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau Assistant Commissioner for Cultural and Creative Industries (1) Deputy Commissioner for Tourism, Tourism Commission Principal Education Officer (Curriculum Development)1, Education Bureau Assistant Director (Heritage and Museums), Leisure and Cultural Services Department *Newly appointed member Terms of Reference To advise the Director of Leisure and Cultural Services on a wide range of subject matters concerning the public museums and related offices managed by the LCSD: positioning, image-building and branding; business development strategies including but not limited to acquisition and use of museum collections, organisation of exhibitions and education programmes, identification of research projects, sponsorship and partnership initiatives; marketing and publicity strategies on the promotion of the museums locally, in the Chinese Mainland and overseas; development of community engagement strategies to reach out to a wider community and stakeholders (e.g. local artists, collectors, local and overseas museums, cultural organisations, and educational institutions); measures to strengthen the operational efficiency and accountability of public museums; and any other matters as proposed by the LCSD. items.title: SFST's opening remarks at APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting 2026 seminars (English only) (with photo)
items.description: Following are the opening remarks by the Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, Mr Christopher Hui, at the APEC (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) Finance Ministers' Meeting (FMM) 2026 seminars today (October 20): Honourable guests, distinguished delegates, ladies and gentlemen, Good morning. It is a great pleasure of mine to welcome you all to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), and to this seminar session held in connection with the APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting 2026. It is especially meaningful for the HKSAR to welcome the FMM to our city for the very first time. We are deeply honoured to contribute to the APEC China Year under the theme, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together", and to facilitate dialogue that advances our shared prosperity across the region. That theme could not be more timely. In an era of profound economic transformation and evolving global challenges, prosperity will not be secured by any economy acting alone. It will be built through partnership, innovation and resilience. I am therefore delighted that this seminar brings together regulators, business leaders and experts from across the Asia-Pacific region for meaningful exchanges on how we can unlock new opportunities, strengthen financial resilience, and drive sustainable growth for all. My sincere thanks go to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and the APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC) Hong Kong, China for organising today's seminars and for their unwavering support. The HKMA, as our central bank and also a steward of monetary and financial stability, is a driving force behind the development of our financial infrastructure ecosystem. ABAC, on the other hand, serves as an important bridge between the public and private sectors, providing APEC leaders with valuable business perspectives on regional co-operation. Its voice helps ensure that our policies remain connected with the realities and aspirations of the business community. Together, these seminars provide a valuable opportunity for the business community to contribute directly to the broader discussions of the FMM, bringing market insights, practical experience and fresh perspectives to the table. Today's discussions will centre on two highly important themes: trade and supply chain finance, and green and sustainable finance. These themes are not only relevant to the region's development, they are also closely aligned with the HKSAR Government's latest policy direction. In our inaugural Five-Year Plan (First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030)), we set out a clear vision to advance "Finance+" so that finance can better serve the real economy. Under "Finance + Trade", we are stepping up support for small and medium-sized enterprises. In this regard, the HKMA has been playing a pivotal role through various initiatives and innovative financing solutions like its Project CargoX. Rather than getting ahead of the discussion, I shall leave it to our speakers to share their insights on these exciting developments. Under "Finance + Green Development", we are making a resolute push to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance and advance an international carbon market. A prime example is the collaboration between the HKEX (Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited)'s Core Climate and the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to explore Hong Kong's participation in cross-boundary carbon trading. In doing so, we may leverage our financial strength as a premier international financial centre to support our country in building a carbon market of greater international influence, thus creating a powerful engine for global environmental sustainability. Beyond these areas, the Five-Year Plan also sets out a clear vision to reinforce Hong Kong's roles as a global offshore Renminbi business hub, an international asset and wealth management centre, and an international risk management centre. We are also committed to developing a commodity trading ecosystem with gold as an entry point. Together, these strengths position Hong Kong as a premier platform connecting capital, enterprises and opportunities across the region and beyond. I am particularly pleased that we are joined today by an outstanding line-up of speakers and practitioners. Their insights have been shaped not only by knowledge, but also by experience at the very forefront of their respective fields. I personally look forward to their sharing and to the vibrant discussions that are to follow. Last but not least, while you are here for the FMM, I warmly invite you to venture beyond the meeting rooms and feel the unique vibe of the many sides of Hong Kong. From our rich Chinese cultural heritage and local traditions to our renowned food culture and dynamic city life, I hope you will have wonderful memories and enjoy the captivating spirit that makes Hong Kong a truly special and beautiful place. With that, may I wish the seminars and the FMM every success, and all of you a fruitful and thoroughly enjoyable stay in Hong Kong. Thank you.

items.title: First-round matching of Co-prosper HK now open for project proponents to submit proposals
items.description: The Government announced today (October 20) the launch of the Co-prosper HK - Welfare Projects Matching Platform (the Platform), and invites social welfare organisations and social enterprises interested in joining the first round of matching to submit proposals by November 29, 2026. The First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) proposes promoting an institutionalised model of tripartite collaboration among the Government, the business sector, and the community in poverty alleviation. In addition, the Chief Executive proposed in the 2026 Policy Address that the Government spearhead the establishment of a matching platform to enable the matching of resources from the business sector with community social welfare projects. To this end, the Commission on Targeted Poverty Alleviation has set up the Platform, through which the business sector's goodwill will be pooled together and matched with the community's creativity to enable the delivery of more targeted projects for disadvantaged groups in need. The Platform serves as a bridge, setting out the target groups and themes, and fostering matching between funders (the business sector) and project proponents (social welfare organisations and social enterprises). Both parties will jointly determine the collaboration model and specific arrangements, and funds will be disbursed directly by the funders to the proponents without being transferred through the Platform. Project proposals for the first round of matching have to target subdivided unit households, single-parent households, all-elderly households, and/or carers as service recipients, and meet at least one of the following themes: (a) respite support; (b) emotional and health support; (c) improvement of living environment and safety enhancement; (d) child-care support; (e) neighbourhood mutual support; (f) nutrition and dietary support; (g) digital inclusion and information empowerment; (h) applications of gerontechnology and care technology; and (i) active ageing. Proponents intending to submit project proposals shall submit them via the electronic form on the following website: https://www.commissiononpoverty.gov.hk/eng/Co-ProsperHK.html by 11.59pm on November 29, 2026. Selection of proponents' project proposals will be conducted by the Working Group on Co-prosper HK - Welfare Projects Matching Platform under the Commission on Targeted Poverty Alleviation. The proponents of selected projects will be invited to attend matching and exchange events to interact and engage with funders, and refine their proposals with a view to entering into collaboration arrangements. Meanwhile, the Working Group is inviting business organisations, family offices, charitable trusts or foundations, among others, to join the Platform as funders.

items.title: Property owner fined over $250,000 for persistently not complying with removal order
items.description: ​An owner was convicted and fined $255,800 in total, of which $155,880 was the fine for the number of days that the offence continued, at the Tuen Mun Magistrates' Courts last Friday (October 16) for persistently failing to comply with a removal order issued under the Buildings Ordinance (BO) (Cap. 123). The case involved unauthorised building works (UBWs) at a detached house on Yu Chui Street, Tai Lam, comprising illegal site formation works for constructing an unauthorised platform of about 122 square metres on a slope adjoining an approved garden, the erection of a floor slab over a void adjacent to an approved dining room, the removal of parts of external walls and the construction of unauthorised structures to extend the floors at different levels of the building with a total floor area of about 57 sq m. As the UBWs were carried out without prior approval and consent from the Buildings Department (BD), a removal order was served on the owner under section 24(1) of the BO. Failing to comply with the removal order, the owner had been prosecuted by the BD seven times and was fined and had sentenced to four months' imprisonment suspended for two years upon convictions by the court. As the owner persisted in not complying with the removal order, the owner was prosecuted for the eighth time. A spokesman for the BD said today (October 20), "UBWs may lead to serious consequences. Owners must comply with removal orders without delay. The BD will continue to take stringent enforcement action and instigate prosecutions against owners again if they persist in not complying with removal orders, so as to ensure building and public safety." Failure to comply with a removal order without reasonable excuse is a serious offence under the BO. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $200,000 and one year's imprisonment, and a further fine of up to $20,000 for each day that the offence continues.

items.title: Departments enhance measures to cope with inbound passenger traffic peak at Huanggang Port
items.description: The Security Bureau (SB) said today (October 19) that southbound passenger flow at the Huanggang Port began to build up from 2pm. Between 2pm and 4pm, about 9 401 passengers arrived in Hong Kong via the Huanggang Port, representing an increase of 366 per cent (more than 3.5 times) compared with the same period previously at the Huanggang Port/Lok Ma Chau Control Point. Southbound passenger traffic is expected to increase further later today. The Immigration Department (ImmD) has disseminated the latest waiting time information via the SB's "Easy Boundary" platform. Before travelling, passengers may check the latest immigration information of various boundary control points, including the Huanggang Port, on the "Easy Boundary" platform. Earlier today, the ImmD also released a short video on social media urging eligible members of the public who plan to cross the boundary at the Huanggang Port to enrol in advance for the "collaborative inspection" automated channels and avoid making their journeys during peak periods, so as to facilitate trip planning and preparation for clearance. All clearance channels at the arrival hall on L4 of the Huanggang Port have been opened. To further expedite passenger flow, the ImmD will implement crowd diversion and control measures on L4 and L2 in collaboration with the Police depending on actual passenger flow. If passenger flow continues to increase, the Police will make necessary arrangements for passengers who have completed immigration clearance to wait for public transport in designated queuing areas in a safe and orderly manner. Members of the public may have to wait briefly in the queuing areas before boarding public transport to leave the port. To cope with today's inbound peak, the Transport Department (TD) has arranged about 120 franchised buses, 40 green minibuses and 130 cross-boundary coaches for service and standby support. During peak hours, the service of franchised buses can be enhanced to every two to three minutes, while the frequency of green minibuses and cross-boundary coaches can be increased to every three to four minutes. Franchised bus operators have also operated individual special short-haul services to expedite the dispersal of inbound passengers and speed up bus turnaround. Meanwhile, service ambassadors and staff of public transport operators station at the L2 hall and the public transport interchange to assist passengers in choosing suitable transport modes according to their destinations and boarding in an orderly manner. Police officers have also been deployed on-site to help maintain order. ​The SB will continue to work with the ImmD, the Police, the TD and other relevant departments to monitor the situation at the port and the passenger flow in real time, flexibly deploy manpower and adopt corresponding contingency measures as necessary to ensure the smooth operation of various clearance arrangements and public transport services. The SB appeals to members of the public to plan their journeys in advance, choose suitable boundary control points and avoid making their journeys during peak periods.

items.title: CHP records case of severe paediatric influenza infection
items.description: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (October 19) recorded a severe paediatric influenza infection case. The CHP urged the public to receive vaccinations as early as possible to safeguard their own health and that of their families. In addition, the public should maintain good personal and environmental hygiene at all times to prevent influenza and other respiratory illnesses. The case involves a six-year-old girl with good past health. She developed a fever, runny nose, vomiting and poor appetite on October 15. She was then brought to the Accident and Emergency Department of Tuen Mun Hospital for medical attention and was admitted for treatment. Her condition deteriorated and was transferred to the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) of the hospital for further treatment on October 17. Her respiratory specimen tested positive for influenza A (H1) virus. Her clinical diagnosis was influenza A infection complicated with shock. The patient remains hospitalised at the PICU in critical condition. The CHP's preliminary investigation revealed that the patient had no travel history during the incubation period, and has not received the 2026/27 Seasonal Influenza Vaccination (SIV). Her household contacts are currently asymptomatic. The CHP will continue to investigate the case. "Hong Kong entered the influenza season in late June this year and the influenza season has lasted for more than three months by now. Currently, the local influenza activity remains at a high level. The predominant influenza virus detected at present is influenza A (H1). The CHP's epidemiological investigation indicated that the characteristics of severe or death cases related to seasonal influenza during this influenza season are similar to those in previous years, affecting primarily the elderly and children. Since the start of the influenza season in late June, a cumulative total of 24 cases of severe paediatric influenza infection have been recorded. Among these cases, 20 patients have recovered and been discharged from hospital, three patients are in critical condition and one has passed away. Due to widespread influenza transmission in the community in recent months, there has been a significant increase in both the number of infections and severe cases. Since the new school year started in September, nearly 440 influenza-like illness outbreaks have been recorded in schools, affecting a total of approximately 2 700 persons. Schools and parents must remain vigilant and take preventive measures. The CHP anticipates that the influenza activity will continue to fluctuate at high levels in the coming weeks," said the Controller of the CHP, Dr Edwin Tsui. The 2026/27 SIV Programmes, including the SIV School Outreach Programme (SIVSOP), commenced on September 17. The SIVSOP this year has introduced a new Electronic Consent Form (e-consent form) feature via eHealth. This new measure not only facilitates the public to join the SIV Programmes but also streamlines the administrative procedures for healthcare service providers and schools, so that SIV outreach activities can start as early as possible. About 840 schools have organised SIV outreach activities. SIV outreach activities are expected to be completed by mid-December, about two weeks earlier than last year. Dr Tsui appeals to all schools and parents in Hong Kong to work closely with the CHP and complete the consent process as soon as possible so that students can be arranged to receive SIV earlier. Dr Tsui reminds parents that the health condition of children with influenza can deteriorate rapidly. Parents must pay close attention to their condition, and visit an accident and emergency department immediately if the child's condition deteriorates with symptoms such as shortness of breath, wheezing, blue lips, chest pain, confusion, a persistent fever or convulsions. Members of the public should seek medical attention as soon as possible if they develop respiratory symptoms. If they live with members of high-risk groups, such as children, the elderly and those with underlying illnesses or compromised immune systems, they should wear a surgical mask at home to reduce the risk of infecting them. Other effective ways to reduce the spread of the disease include maintaining household hygiene, frequently cleaning and disinfecting frequently touched surfaces, practising good hand hygiene, and ensuring proper indoor air circulation. Members of the public may refer to the CHP's COVID-19 & Flu Express , Seasonal Influenza Webpage and Vaccination Schemes for the latest information.

items.title: Director of Health attends WHO Western Pacific Regional Committee meeting (with photos)
items.description: The Director of Health, Dr Ronald Lam, today (October 19) led a delegation from the Department of Health (DH) to attend the 77th session of the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Committee for the Western Pacific in Manila, the Philippines. He engaged in in-depth discussions with representatives from other countries and regions on major health issues of common concern. They explored practical response strategies and effective ways to strengthen the resilience of health systems. During the opening session today, Dr Lam reported on the latest developments and challenges in public health in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR). He said, "The latest progress report announced by the WHO shows that the Western Pacific Region's Universal Health Coverage index has risen significantly, with particularly notable progress in communicable disease prevention and control, demonstrating the powerful force of regional collaboration. The HKSAR is committed to maintaining a resilient public health system, including accessible healthcare services, comprehensive disease prevention and control, surveillance and early warning, and emergency response and preparedness. As a result, the HKSAR has consistently ranked among the world's best in core health indicators, such as life expectancy, and maternal and infant mortality rates. However, like other economies in the region, the HKSAR faces a number of public health challenges, such as the growing burden posed by non-communicable diseases, healthcare workforce, communicable diseases, and climate-related health risks. The HKSAR is actively leveraging digital health tools and artificial intelligence to optimise resource allocation and enhance the efficiency of primary healthcare. We are adopting a 'life-course approach' to ensure that our public health measures protect all people, especially the vulnerable." The Chief Executive recently announced the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) (Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan) and the Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address (Policy Address), providing a strategic vision for a bright new era and enhancing livelihood. In terms of healthcare, three key directions are covered, including deepening healthcare system reform, developing Hong Kong into a health and medical innovation hub with global influence, and playing the role of a healthcare 'superconnector' for the HKSAR to deepen cross-boundary healthcare co-operation, align with national standards and deepen international co-operation. Dr Lam added, "The WHO Western Pacific Region's vision of 'Weaving Health for All' closely aligns with the strategic development directions and objectives on healthcare outlined in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address. Hong Kong, China, will continue to collaborate closely with the WHO, leveraging the advantage under 'one country, two systems' to continuously deepen exchanges and co-operation on health with various regions, deeply participate in global health governance, and make positive contributions to improving the health and well-being of people around the world." During the meeting, participants will also discuss artificial intelligence, hypertension control, immunisation, tobacco control, as well as regional health essential stockpile and pooled procurement mechanism, among other topics. With the continued support of the National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China, the DH has actively integrated into and served the national health development framework, actively supporting the WHO in advancing global health issues and addressing various public health challenges, contributing to global public health. The DH has been designated by the WHO as a Collaborating Centre for Smoking Cessation and Treatment of Tobacco Dependence and a Collaborating Centre for Traditional Medicine for over ten consecutive years. The DH also serves as a reference laboratory for various communicable diseases, contributing to global disease surveillance and talent training. Dr Lam added that the Microbiology Division of the Public Health Laboratory Services Branch under the Centre for Health Protection of the DH was appointed by the WHO this year as a "Collaborating Centre on Quality and Capacity Building for the Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System", and has successively hosted international expert meetings on WHO's surveillance, response, and prevention and control of global influenza, and on the formulation of the International Herbal Pharmacopoeia, fully demonstrating the HKSAR's important bridging role in the healthcare field and its contribution to improving global health governance. With the support of the Central Government and under the principle of "one country, two systems", the DH will continue to maintain close liaison with the WHO member states and regions on various issues concerning the protection of public health. Through multilateral collaboration and consensus-building, the DH will further enhance and safeguard overall public health in the region.

items.title: DH announces latest situation regarding Legionnaires' disease cases
items.description: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) today (October 19) reported the latest number of Legionnaires' disease (LD) cases, and reminded the public of the importance of using and maintaining properly designed man-made water systems, adding that susceptible groups should strictly observe relevant precautions. From October 11 to October 17, the CHP recorded three community-acquired LD cases, involving three males aged between 44 and 67. Details are as follows: a 44-year-old male with history of smoking living in Tai Po District; a 59-year-old male with underlying illnesses living in Kwai Tsing District; and a 67-year-old male with underlying illnesses living in Tai Po District. ​The CHP is conducting epidemiological investigations to identify the potential sources of infection and high-risk exposure. An initial investigation revealed that the aforesaid cases are sporadic cases. No epidemiological linkages have been established between these cases and other confirmed cases previously recorded in Hong Kong. As of October 17, 160 LD cases had been recorded this year. In 2025 and 2024, there were 167 and 135 LD cases respectively. Men, people aged over 50, smokers, alcoholics and persons with weakened immunity are more susceptible to LD. Some situations may also increase the risk of infection, including poor maintenance of water systems; living in areas with old water systems, cooling towers or fountains; using electric water heaters, whirlpool spas or hot water spring spas; and recent stays in hotels or ships. Legionellae are found in various environmental settings and grow well in warm water (20 to 45 degrees Celsius). They can be found in aqueous environments such as water tanks, hot and cold water systems, cooling towers, whirlpool spas, water fountains, humidifiers and home respiratory devices that support breathing. People may become infected when they breathe in contaminated droplets (aerosols) and mist generated by artificial water systems, or when handling garden soil, compost and potting mixes. Immunocompromised persons should: Use sterile or boiled water for drinking, tooth brushing and mouth rinsing; Avoid using humidifiers, or other mist- or aerosol-generating devices; and If using humidifiers, or other mist- or aerosol-generating devices, fill the water tank with only sterile or cooled freshly boiled water, and not water directly from the tap. Also, clean and maintain humidifiers/devices regularly according to manufacturers' instructions. Never leave stagnant water in a humidifier/device. Empty the water tank, wipe all surfaces dry, and change the water daily. ​The public should observe the health advice below: Observe personal hygiene; Do not smoke and avoid alcohol consumption; Strainers in water taps and shower heads should be inspected, cleaned, descaled and disinfected regularly or at a frequency recommended by the manufacturer; If a fresh-water plumbing system is properly maintained, it is not necessary to install domestic water filters. Use of water filters is not encouraged as clogging occurs easily, which can promote growth of micro-organisms. In case water filters are used, the pore size should be 0.2 micrometres (µm) or less and the filter needs to be changed periodically according to the manufacturer's recommendations; Drain and clean water tanks of buildings at least quarterly; Drain or purge for at least one minute infrequently used water outlets (e.g. water taps, shower heads and hot water outlets) and stagnant points of the pipework weekly or before use; Seek and follow doctors' professional advice regarding the use and maintenance of home respiratory devices and use only sterile water (not distilled or tap water) to clean and fill the reservoir. Clean and maintain the device regularly according to the manufacturer's instructions. After cleaning/disinfection, rinse the device with sterile water, cooled freshly boiled water or water filtered with 0.2 µm filters. Never leave stagnant water in the device. Empty the water tank, keep all surfaces dry, and change the water daily; and When handling garden soil, compost and potting mixes: Wear gloves and a face mask; Water gardens and compost gently using low pressure; Open composted potting mixes slowly and make sure the opening is directed away from the face; Wet the soil to reduce dust when potting plants; and Avoid working in poorly ventilated places such as enclosed greenhouses. The public may visit the CHP's LD page , the Code of Practice for Prevention of LD and the Housekeeping Guidelines for Cold and Hot Water Systems for Building Management of the Prevention of LD Committee, and the CHP's risk-based strategy for prevention and control of LD. Additionally, as smokers and alcoholics are more susceptible to LD, the Government urges members of the public to quit smoking and avoid drinking. Members of the public may call the DH Integrated Smoking Cessation Hotline at 1833 183, which is answered by registered nurses who provide professional counselling and referrals to a wide range of free smoking cessation services. The public may also visit the smoking cessation thematic website ( www.livetobaccofree.hk ) for more information on smoking cessation. The DH has also developed and promulgated the Alcohol Screening and Brief Intervention tool to primary healthcare service providers to facilitate the early identification and management of at-risk drinkers. For information on alcohol-related harm, please visit the DH's Change for Health website .

items.title: HKTE organises career fair in London with Hong Kong and Chinese Mainland enterprises (with photos)
items.description: Hong Kong Talent Engage (HKTE) held the "Hong Kong • Global Talent & Career Showcase" (the showcase) in London, the United Kingdom (UK), on October 17 and 18 (London time) to introduce to local international talent the career prospects in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland so as to attract them to come to pursue their development. The showcase was supported by the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Development Office and the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in London. More than 50 enterprises and organisations from Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland offered over 200 job vacancies across sectors such as banking and finance, innovation and technology, engineering and construction, and professional services at the showcase. The showcase attracted more than 4 500 visits. It also featured a forum and workshops, at which government representatives and business leaders introduced Hong Kong's development advantages, talent landscape and market trends, and senior human resources representatives offered practical job-seeking tips and career planning insights. ​ In his welcome remarks, the Director of HKTE, Mr Felix Chan, said that the showcase enabled global talent to learn about career development in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland, and exchange and match jobs directly with enterprises. He added that, in line with Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, HKTE will continue to promote Hong Kong around the world and adopt a targeted approach to attract talent with the skills required for the development of our country and Hong Kong. ​ The Commissioner for the Development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, Miss Pamela Lam, said in her keynote speech that Hong Kong's First Five-year Plan clearly states that Hong Kong will participate in the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) into an international first-class bay area and a world class city cluster with global influence. Among these efforts, the Northern Metropolis is a main platform for Hong Kong to deeply engage in the development of the GBA, and to actively integrate into and serve the overall national development. It is also the driving force behind Hong Kong's future development. She added that the Northern Metropolis will foster the integrated development of education, technology, industry, talent and urban development, which is bound to generate immense opportunities. She encouraged local talent to pursue their careers in Hong Kong, establish a base in the city and tap into opportunities in the GBA. ​ The Director-General of the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in London, Miss Fiona Chau, said at the forum that Hong Kong is an ideal springboard for UK professionals, entrepreneurs and graduates to explore Asian markets. The showcase enabled participants to deepen their understanding of the job markets in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland, and she hoped that they would seize the opportunity to pursue development in Hong Kong. ​ A representative from a participating enterprise said that the event enabled enterprises to connect with global talent directly and identify suitable candidates with international perspective and cross-cultural collaboration experience, thereby supporting business expansion. ​ In the coming year, HKTE will visit key regions including the Chinese Mainland, Asia Pacific, Europe and North America to conduct promotional activities. items.title: CE meets President of AIIB (with photo)
items.description: The Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, met with the President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), Ms Zou Jiayi, at Government House today (October 19) to exchange views on further strengthening regional financial co-operation. The Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, Mr Christopher Hui, also attended the meeting. Mr Lee welcomed Ms Zou and her delegation to Hong Kong for the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Finance Ministers' Meeting 2026. He said that the AIIB has all along supported developing economies in improving infrastructure and promoting sustainable economic development, and Hong Kong, as a member of the AIIB, has been actively supporting the AIIB's work. With the announcement of Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address last month, Hong Kong will continue to consolidate and enhance its financial strengths, strengthen development in areas including green finance, financial technology and offshore Renminbi business, which will help support the AIIB's project financing, fundraising and financial management to promote the sustainable development of infrastructure in Asia. Mr Lee said that Hong Kong is one of the world's leading international financial centres. It continues to come first as the world's freest economy and ranks third globally and first in Asia in the Global Financial Centres Index. With its vibrant capital market, world-class professional services and diversified financial products, Hong Kong is well placed to provide flexible capital allocation support for the AIIB's projects such as those relating to carbon neutrality and green economic transformation. Mr Lee added that the AIIB's issuance of Hong Kong dollar bonds in Hong Kong in recent years is a testament to the achievements of financial co-operation between the two sides. He welcomed the AIIB's continued use of Hong Kong's strengths as an international financial hub and its mature and comprehensive bond market to connect with investors around the world and empower projects with added value. Mr Lee said that he is pleased that the AIIB will soon establish in Hong Kong an office serving both financing and operational functions, demonstrating Hong Kong's role as a gateway connecting the country and the world. He believed that the establishment of the office will create more opportunities for the local financial sector and deepen co-operation and exchanges between the two sides. The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government will fully support the establishment and operation of the office, giving full play to Hong Kong's role as a "super connector" and "super value-adder" to facilitate the AIIB's business expansion. He expressed the hope that both sides will continue to work together to strengthen collaboration in areas such as transition finance, technology and innovation and talent development to jointly promote regional economic prosperity.

items.title: Latest updates on passenger traffic at Huanggang Port (with photos)
items.description: ​The Security Bureau (SB) today (October 18) said that outbound passenger flow at the Huanggang Port had increased significantly since around 11am this morning. Around 19 000 passengers departed for the Mainland via the Huanggang Port between 12 noon and 2pm, representing an increase of 835 per cent (over eight times) compared with the same period in the past at the Huanggang Port/Lok Ma Chau Control Point. During the peak hour between 1pm and 2pm, as many as 9 728 outbound passenger trips were recorded within one hour, representing an increase of 899 per cent (nearly nine times) compared with the same period in the past at the Huanggang Port/Lok Ma Chau Control Point. In view of this, the Immigration Department (ImmD) immediately opened all clearance channels and counters at the departure hall on L5 to expedite passenger flow, and implemented crowd diversion and control measures on L2 and L5 in collaboration with the Police. For passengers entering the Huanggang Port during the peak hours mentioned above, the waiting time for crowd diversion arrangements on L2 was about 30 to 45 minutes, while the waiting time inside the departure hall on L5 was maintained within 30 minutes. The ImmD has disseminated the latest waiting time information via the "Easy Boundary" platform, and advised members of the public and travellers to plan their journeys in advance and consider using other boundary control points for departure. The outbound peak gradually subsided from around 2pm today. Crowd diversion and control measures on L2 were lifted at 2.10pm, and the waiting time at the departure hall on L5 had dropped to under 15 minutes by 2.40pm. In fact, relevant departments had already assessed the potential surge in passenger flow during peak hours and formulated plans for diversion, queue management and inter-departmental co-ordination during an earlier large-scale drill at the Huanggang Port involving around 20 000 participants. Faced with this sudden surge in passengers, the various contingency plans were activated promptly and overall operations remained generally smooth. The SB will continue to work with the ImmD, the Police and other relevant departments to closely monitor the situation at the port and passenger flow. Timely reviews will be conducted and corresponding contingency measures will be adopted in light of actual circumstances to ensure the smooth operation of clearance arrangements and public services.

Mr Ng had held such important positions as member of the Preparatory Committee of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and Hong Kong Affairs Adviser, making sterling contributions to the smooth process of Hong Kong's return to the motherland and the maintenance of the city's long-term stability and prosperity. Over the years, Mr Ng served as Principal and Supervisor of Pui Kiu Middle School, and as Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Pui Kiu Education Foundation, nurturing generations of students with great dedication. He dedicated his life to patriotic education and had cultivated a wealth of outstanding talent for the country and Hong Kong. He was an extraordinary educationalist with remarkable contributions. items.title: CHP investigates fatal case of invasive pneumococcal disease
items.description: ​The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) is today (October 18) investigating a fatal case of invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD), and reminded the public to observe hygiene practices against the disease. The patient was a nine-year-old boy with good past health, who had developed fever, runny nose, cough, and chest pain associated with the coughing since October 10. He was brought to private clinics on October 10 and 13. On October 14, he was brought to the Accident and Emergency Department at Tin Shui Wai Hospital due to persistent symptoms and shortness of breath. He was transferred to the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit at Tuen Mun Hospital for further management. His condition deteriorated and he passed away on October 15. His pleural fluid specimen tested positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae upon laboratory testing. The clinical diagnosis was severe pneumonia complicated with empyema, septic shock and acute renal failure. The CHP will arrange further testing and serotype analysis of patient's bacterial samples. Initial enquiries revealed that the boy had no travel history during the incubation period. His home contacts have remained asymptomatic so far. Investigations are ongoing. The case will be referred to the Coroner for investigation. Pneumococcal infection is caused by the bacteria Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus). It causes a wide range of diseases. More common ones include middle ear infection and chest infection. It may also cause various forms of IPDs, such as infection of the brain membranes and blood stream. The infection can be serious or even life-threatening. Local data showed that about three per cent of the cases of paediatric IPD recorded over the past decade have been fatal. Pneumococci are commonly found in the nose and throat of healthy people, particularly in children. Occasionally, these bacteria will cause an infection. They mainly spread through droplets via coughing and sneezing, close contact with the patients or contact with materials soiled with the bacteria. Scientific research data from around the world indicated that the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) can provide direct protection effectively, and achieve herd immunity by reducing transmission. Receiving PCV can reduce the risk of IPD among children by 60 per cent to 90 per cent, demonstrating the effectiveness of the vaccine. In light of this, the DH has incorporated PCV into the Hong Kong Childhood Immunisation Programme (HKCIP) since September 2009, providing free vaccinations for children. Local research data showed a significant decrease in the number of cases of IPD after the HKCIP was launched. The incidence of children aged two years or below, and children aged two to five years dropped by 85 per cent and 35 per cent respectively. Parents should ensure that their children receive PCV according to the schedule of the HKCIP. Elderly and high-risk individuals should also receive pneumococcal vaccine to safeguard their health. The health condition of children with IPD can deteriorate rapidly. Parents should bring their children to seek medical attention as soon as possible if they develop a fever or respiratory symptoms. If the condition persists or deteriorates with symptoms such as shortness of breath, chest pain, blue lips, convulsions, drowsiness, stiff neck, refusal to eat, persistent vomiting or decreased urination, they should attend an accident and emergency department for treatment immediately. To prevent pneumococcal infection, the CHP appealed to the public for pneumococcal vaccination and hygiene practices. The public may visit the CHP's invasive pneumococcal disease page for more information.

items.title: Hong Kong Customs detects two drug trafficking cases involving incoming passengers at airport (with photos)
items.description: Hong Kong Customs detected two drug trafficking cases involving passengers at Hong Kong International Airport for two consecutive days (October 17 and 18) and seized about 5.4 kilograms of suspected cocaine, 17kg of suspected cannabis buds and 15 suspected Alprazolam tablets, with a total estimated market value of about $6.8 million. In the first case, a 40-year-old Mainland male passenger arrived in Hong Kong from São Paulo, Brazil, via Istanbul, Turkey, yesterday (October 17). During customs clearance, Customs officers found the batch of suspected cocaine with an estimated market value of about $3.3 million inside his carry-on baggage. He was subsequently arrested. In the second case, a 52-year-old Mainland female passenger arrived in Hong Kong from Bangkok, Thailand, today (October 18). During customs clearance, Customs officers found the batch of suspected cannabis buds with an estimated market value of about $3.5 million in her check-in suitcase, and 15 suspected Alprazolam tablets in her carry-on backpack. The woman was subsequently arrested. Investigation of the two cases is ongoing. Customs will continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking activities through intelligence analysis. The department also reminds members of the public to stay alert and not participate in drug trafficking activities for monetary return. They must not accept hiring or delegation from another party to carry controlled items into and out of Hong Kong. They are also reminded not to carry unknown items for other people. Customs will continue to apply a risk assessment approach and focus on selecting passengers from high-risk regions for clearance to combat transnational drug trafficking activities. Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $5 million and life imprisonment. Members of the public may report any suspected drug trafficking activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form ( eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: FEHD reminds public to comply with regulations when dining out with dogs during Halloween
items.description: With Halloween approaching, the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) today (October 18) reminded members of the public who plan to bring their dogs along when dining out to confirm in advance whether the restaurant concerned is permitted to admit dogs and to comply with the relevant law and regulations. At present, over 990 restaurants hold permits allowing dogs to enter. Persons-in-charge of these restaurants must ensure that their premises comply with the relevant licensing conditions and statutory requirements, step up staff supervision and remind customers bringing dogs of the relevant requirements, so as to safeguard public safety and hygiene. A spokesman for the FEHD stressed that both restaurant operators and dog owners have the responsibility to comply with the relevant regulations. Restaurants without permission must observe the law and must not allow customers to bring dogs onto their premises. Members of the public who bring dogs into non-permitted restaurants also commit an offence. The department will continue to conduct risk-based inspections and take enforcement action against any irregularities. The spokesman added that, since the measure of allowing dogs to enter permitted restaurants was implemented on July 9, the FEHD has assisted the trade and members of the public in complying with the relevant requirements through ongoing inspections, publicity and education. Following the initial one-month adaptation period, the department has adopted a pragmatic and flexible enforcement strategy, conducting risk-based inspections to strike an appropriate balance between promoting pet inclusivity and safeguarding food safety and public hygiene. Regarding restaurants which unlawfully allow dogs to enter, the FEHD has, to date, initiated 20 prosecutions against offending restaurants and seven prosecutions against persons who unlawfully brought dogs into such restaurants. In addition, the FEHD has taken stringent enforcement action against serious breaches committed by customers bringing dogs to permitted restaurants, including four prosecutions for failing to keep dogs securely on a leash. The spokesman reiterated that permitted restaurants must strictly comply with the law and licensing conditions. These include prohibiting open-flame cooking at dining tables; refusing entry of fighting dogs or known dangerous dogs; and forbidding dogs access to food rooms. At all times while in a restaurant, a dog must be securely held by an adult on a leash not exceeding 1.5 metres in length, or securely tethered to a fixture. Dog owners must also ensure that their dogs are properly controlled at all times. The FEHD will take decisive enforcement action against any violations. The FEHD again appealed to restaurants and customers to comply with the law and the relevant requirements, fulfil their respective responsibilities and help maintain a pleasant dining environment and public hygiene, thereby promoting pet inclusivity. Members of the public may visit the FEHD's dedicated webpage ( www.fehd.gov.hk/english/licensing/dog_restaurants/dog_restaurants_list.html ) for relevant information and the full list of permitted restaurants.

items.title: Commissioner for Development of Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area promotes GBA opportunities and Hong Kong's strengths in London (with photos)
items.description: The Commissioner for the Development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, Miss Pamela Lam, concluded a four-day visit to London, the United Kingdom (UK) on October 17 (London time). During her visit, Miss Lam took part in a series of events covering talent recruitment, economic and trade promotion, cultural industries and youth development to promote Hong Kong's strengths and the development opportunities of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), as well as Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan. During the visit, Miss Lam attended the "Hong Kong • Global Talent & Career Showcase" organised by Hong Kong Talent Engage to introduce GBA opportunities and Hong Kong's strengths. In her keynote speech, she said that Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan clearly states that Hong Kong will continue to participate in the development of the GBA into an international first-class bay area with global influence. Among the initiatives, the Northern Metropolis serves as the main platform for Hong Kong to deeply engage in the development of the GBA, and to actively integrate into and serve overall national development. The Hong Kong Park in the Hetao Shenzhen‑Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Co‑operation Zone is a cross-boundary co-operation platform that is a key national development priority, where enterprises and international professionals can leverage Hong Kong's internationalised innovation and technology (I&T) research and business environment to gain easy access to the industrial chains and markets of Shenzhen and other GBA cities, bringing unprecedented opportunities for global talent. Miss Lam also attended a business luncheon jointly organised by the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Development Office (GBA Office) and the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in London. She briefed representatives from the business sector, including the China-Britain Business Council and the Hong Kong Association, on Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, as well as Hong Kong's outstanding performance in economic freedom, competitiveness and financial markets. She stressed that over the next five years, Hong Kong will consolidate and enhance its traditional strengths, strengthen I&T co-operation and prioritise the Northern Metropolis for future development to open a new chapter for I&T. She encouraged enterprises to leverage Hong Kong's advantage of being closely connected to both the Chinese Mainland and the rest of the world, and to establish a presence in the city to tap into the huge GBA market . On the youth and cultural front, Miss Lam met with Hong Kong students studying in the UK, and introduced the diverse opportunities available for young people across various sectors under the GBA development as set out in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan. She also attended a cocktail reception to promote culture and the arts in the GBA. In her speech, she highlighted that during the National 15th Five-Year Plan period, Hong Kong will continue in its important role as an East-meets-West centre for cultural and artistic exchange. Hong Kong is among the world's top three arts trading centres. The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Government will further expand the scale of Hong Kong's cultural and creative industries. She encouraged collectors, museums, and arts and cultural institutions around the world to make good use of Hong Kong's role as the "super connector" and "super value-adder" to connect with the vast cultural and arts markets and resources in the GBA. While in London, Miss Lam also called on the Minister and Chief of the Economic and Commercial Section of the Chinese Embassy in the UK, Mr Yu Benlin, and briefed him on Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the work of the HKSAR Government in taking forward GBA development. The GBA Office will continue to step up promotion of the opportunities in GBA development and Hong Kong's strengths through overseas visits and by leveraging the international connections of overseas Economic and Trade Offices and partner organisations.

items.title: Secretary for Health attends World Conference on Traditional Medicine 2026 in Beijing (with photos)
items.description: The Secretary for Health, Professor Lo Chung-mau, led a delegation to attend the World Conference on Traditional Medicine 2026 held in Beijing today (October 17) to have in-depth discussions and exchanges with senior health officials from around the world, as well as experts and academics in the traditional medicine field on issues related to traditional medicine, including legislation, policy and regulation, scientific research, talent cultivation, empowerment of artificial intelligence, as well as promotion of integration of traditional medicine into healthcare service systems. The conference is jointly organised by the People's Government of Beijing Municipality, the National Health Commission (NHC), the National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine and the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) in collaboration with the World Health Organization. At the opening ceremony, Professor Lo listened to Premier Li Qiang's keynote speech. Speaking at the panel discussions of the traditional medicine government forum, Professor Lo shared with attendees the strategic direction for integrating Chinese medicine (CM) into the healthcare system in Hong Kong. Professor Lo said, "CM is a treasure of Chinese civilisation. The National 15th Five-Year Plan emphasises the promotion of CM heritage and innovation. It also explicitly calls for improving the CM service system, enhancing primary care-level CM services, and developing integrated Chinese-Western medicine services. To fully align with the country’s vision, the Chief Executive expressly pointed out in the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) (2026-2030) (Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan) and the 2026 Policy Address announced last month that Hong Kong will promote comprehensive, high-quality, and high-standard development of CM, thereby ensuring Hong Kong seamlessly aligns with the national development strategy of building a 'Healthy China'. "The HKSAR Government will step up efforts to promote the development of CM. Through the two flagship institutions, The Chinese Medicine Hospital of Hong Kong (CMHHK) and the Government Chinese Medicines Testing Institute, Hong Kong will strive to promote pure CM and integrated Chinese-Western medicine services as the 'Hong Kong model' in the modern healthcare system. Furthermore, by further advancing local integrated Chinese and Western medicine services and CM talent cultivation, fostering international research collaboration in herb-drug interaction, and establishing rigorous quality standards for Chinese herbal medicines, Hong Kong will fully leverage our role as a bridgehead to provide a high-standard reference model for the world," he added. During the conference, Professor Lo and his delegation met with Vice Minister of the NHC Mr Zheng Zhe, and the Commissioner of the NMPA, Mr Huang Guo, respectively to introduce to them the healthcare-related policies in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address. Professor Lo said to Mr Zheng, "With our high-quality healthcare professionals and highly efficient healthcare system, Hong Kong boasts a number of world-leading health indicators, and is among the regions with the longest life expectancies in the world. Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan is interconnected with the National 15th Five-Year Plan. In line with the strategic initiative of accelerating the building of a 'Healthy China' of the National 15th Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan proposes deepening healthcare system reform, advancing the high-quality development of primary healthcare, and enhancing the resilience of Hong Kong’s healthcare services, thereby building a healthy and vibrant Hong Kong with concerted efforts." He also said, "Building a 'Healthy China' is a major national strategy. In an important speech delivered at the recently convened National Meeting on Health, President Xi Jinping emphasised that the period of the 15th Five-Year Plan is a crucial moment of achieving the goal of building a 'Healthy China' by 2035. To build a balanced, inclusive, high-quality and efficient 'Healthy China', it is necessary to possess six core capabilities in health management, disease prevention and control, healthcare services, health insurance support, health and medical innovation, and talent cultivation. In active alignment with this initiative, the HKSAR Government will advance Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, upholding the principle of prevention first and a health-centred approach to deepen healthcare system reform, develop an international health and medical innovation hub, leverage the role as a 'super connector' in healthcare and build a healthy and vibrant Hong Kong with concerted efforts, hence better integrating into and serving the overall development of a 'Healthy China'." During the meeting with Mr Huang, Professor Lo provided him with details on the latest progress of the establishment of the Hong Kong Centre for Medical Products Regulation (CMPR), including the establishment of the CMPR by the end of this year, the appointment of Mr Li Zili as the Controller for Medical Products Regulation, and the application for accession as a member of the International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use. The CMPR will progressively establish a robust drug approval system, aiming for the full implementation of "primary evaluation" mechanism for new drug registration by 2030, thereby becoming an internationally recognised regulatory authority for medical products. Members of the Hong Kong delegation include the Director of Health, Dr Ronald Lam, and the Controller-designate for Medical Products Regulation, Mr Li Zili, as well as representatives of the Health Bureau, the Department of Health (DH) and the Hospital Authority. The Hospital Chief Executive of CMHHK, Professor Bian Zhaoxiang, also joined the delegation for the conference. Members of the Hong Kong delegation will continue to attend the conference tomorrow (October 18). Professor Lo will participate in the high-level government forum: "Belt and Road Traditional Chinese Medicine Development Conference (Ministerial Level) Roundtable Dialogue" at the conference. A representative of the DH will also share the latest progress regarding the regulation of Chinese medicines during the parallel session of the conference. Professor Lo and his delegation will return to Hong Kong tomorrow afternoon (October 18).

items.description: The Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan, continued his visit to Bangkok, Thailand, this morning (October 17). Mr Chan met with the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of Thailand, Mr Ekniti Nitithanprapas, in the morning to exchange views on further strengthening economic, trade and financial co-operation between Hong Kong and Thailand. The two sides explored ways to deepen co-operation and connect foreign direct investment in Thailand with Hong Kong's capital market to further support enterprises investing and expanding their businesses in Thailand. Mr Chan said that Hong Kong could leverage its strengths as an international financial centre to provide comprehensive investment and financing support for enterprises in Thailand. Hong Kong also welcomed closer regulatory co-operation between the two securities markets to encourage dual listings by enterprises from both places and strengthen capital market ties. With Mainland enterprises accelerating their international expansion and increasing investment in Thailand and Southeast Asia, Hong Kong could further enhance its bridging role by matching the Mainland's technological strengths with Thailand's industrial development needs, thereby fostering investment and industrial co-operation. Mr Chan thanked Mr Ekniti for visiting Hong Kong to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Finance Ministers' Meeting, and invited him to attend the Asian Financial Forum in Hong Kong in January next year to further strengthen economic, trade and financial ties between the two places and across the region, and jointly explore new opportunities for co-operation. Mr Chan also met with the chief executive officer and senior management of a major French bank with extensive operations in Hong Kong this morning. They exchanged views on developments in the fixed income and currency markets in Hong Kong and the region, green and sustainable finance, tokenised financial products, and asset and wealth management. Mr Chan welcomed the group's continued expansion in Hong Kong and its use of the city as a key hub for developing its regional business, tapping into the opportunities offered by Hong Kong as an international financial centre. Having concluded his morning programme, Mr Chan departed for Hong Kong and returned in the afternoon today.

The spokesperson emphasised that non-emergency patients should avoid using Accident and Emergency (A&E) services and instead seek treatment at FMCs, private doctors or 24-hour outpatient services at private hospitals to reduce pressure on public hospital A&Es.
