items.title: Hong Kong Customs special operation combats processing workshops and storages of suspected counterfeit hard disks (with photo)
items.description: Hong Kong Customs mounted a special operation yesterday (October 15) in Tuen Mun to combat processing workshops and storages of suspected counterfeit hard disks, and seized about 6 800 items of suspected counterfeit hard disks with a total estimated market value of about $50 million. Six persons were arrested. After an in-depth investigation by Customs officers and with the assistance of trademark owners, Customs took special operation yesterday and raided five industrial units in Tuen Mun. Five men and one woman were arrested, including five Mainland persons and one local person aged between 31 and 59. Large batches of suspected counterfeit hard disks, packaging materials and tools were seized. In addition, Customs seized approximately 20 000 second-hand hard disks suspected of awaiting processing in the industrial units. It is believed that the arrested persons first purchased large quantities of second-hand hard disks and used items such as adhesive removers to remove the original labels from the second-hand hard disks. They then used specialised hard disk electronic equipment to format the hard disks, and affixed labels of various major brands, sealed them in anti-static bags, and offered them for sale. The arrested persons have been detained for investigation. The investigation is ongoing and the likelihood of further arrests is not ruled out. Customs will continue to step up inspection and enforcement to vigorously combat the sale of different kinds of counterfeit goods. Customs reminds consumers to procure goods at reputable shops and check with the trademark owners or their authorised agents if the authenticity of a product is in doubt. Traders should also be cautious and prudent in merchandising since selling counterfeit goods is a serious crime and offenders are liable to criminal sanctions. Under the Trade Descriptions Ordinance, any person who forges a trademark, sells or possesses for sale any goods with a forged trademark commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $500,000 and imprisonment for five years. Members of the public may report any suspected counterfeiting activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080, its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form (​ eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: CFS finds samples of mung bean starch sheet and its related product not in compliance with requirement on preservative
items.description: The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department announced today (October 16) that samples of two batches of mung bean starch sheet and its related product were found not in compliance with the requirement of the Preservatives in Food Regulation (Cap. 132BD) (the Regulation). The CFS is following up on the incident. Product details are as follows: Product name: (Not available in English) Weight: 500 grams Manufacture dates: June 27, 2026; July 9, 2026 Place of origin: China Sole distributor: Zhuang Ji Food Trade Company A spokesman for the CFS said, "The CFS collected two samples of mung bean starch sheet and its related product sold and supplied by the above-mentioned sole distributor for testing. The test results showed that the two samples contained sodium dehydroacetate at a level of 69 and 61 parts per million respectively, not in compliance with the requirement of the Regulation. Prosecution will be instituted should there be sufficient evidence." "The CFS has informed the vendor concerned of the matter concerned, and instructed it to stop selling and remove from shelves the affected batches of the product concerned, and to initiate a recall. The trade should stop using or selling the affected batches of the product immediately if they possess any of them. Members of the public and the trade may call the distributor's hotline at 3706 5528 during office hours for enquiries about the recall of the affected batches of the product," the spokesman added. According to the Regulation, sodium dehydroacetate is not allowed to be used in mung bean starch sheet. Any person who sells food not in compliance with the requirement on preservatives under the Regulation is liable upon conviction to a fine of $50,000 and imprisonment for six months. The spokesman said that based on the level of sodium dehydroacetate detected in the two samples, risk assessment showed that adverse health effects are unlikely under usual consumption. The CFS has informed the trade, and will continue to follow up on the incident and take appropriate action. The investigation is ongoing.

items.title: Three incoming passengers convicted and jailed for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes and alternative smoking products (with photos)
items.description: Three incoming passengers were sentenced to six to nine months' imprisonment by the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts today (October 16) for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes, failing to declare them to Customs officers, as well as importing alternative smoking products, in contravention of the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (DCO) and the Import and Export Ordinance (IEO). Customs officers intercepted an incoming Mainland male passenger, aged 40, and two incoming Mainland female passengers, aged 42 and 38, at Hong Kong International Airport yesterday (October 15) and seized 146 600 duty-not-paid cigarettes and 6 000 alternative smoking products, with an estimated market value of about $680,000 and a duty potential of about $480,000, from their personal baggage. The three passengers were subsequently arrested. Customs welcomes the sentences. The custodial sentences have imposed a considerable deterrent effect and reflect the seriousness of the offences. Customs reminds members of the public that under the DCO, cigarettes are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who imports, deals with, possesses, sells or buys illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. Under the IEO, any person who imports an alternative smoking product into Hong Kong commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form ( eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: FS attends Annual Meetings of IMF and World Bank Group in Bangkok (with photos/video)
items.description: The Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan, continued his visit to Bangkok, Thailand, today (October 16). As a member of the Chinese delegation, he attended the plenary session of the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group (WBG). He also took part in discussions organised by financial media and a think tank, met with senior executives of international financial institutions and enterprises, and hosted a dinner for financial sector leaders to highlight Hong Kong's development opportunities and promote financial and investment co-operation. At a fireside chat organised by Bloomberg, Mr Chan outlined how Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan aligns with the National 15th Five-Year Plan, providing clear development directions and goals for the public and businesses. He said that Hong Kong would focus on developing the "four centres and one hub", reinforcing and enhancing its status as an international financial, shipping and trade centre. Hong Kong would also leverage its strengths and work in tandem with other cities in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) to advance its development as an innovation and technology (I&T) centre. Mr Chan stressed that financial development must serve the real economy. Hong Kong would deepen its "Finance+" strategy to empower different industries, support enterprises in upgrading and transformation, and provide venture capital, patient capital and long-term funding for I&T to accelerate the development of emerging industries. Hong Kong would also continue to broaden its financial products and services, develop commodities trading, enhance its listing regime and further facilitate financing for technology enterprises. To meet the needs of Mainland enterprises expanding overseas and reorganising their production and supply chains, Hong Kong would provide comprehensive support covering logistics, supply chain management, trade finance, risk management and professional services. The Government would also proactively address enterprises' needs through cross-departmental collaboration. He said that Hong Kong's international character is a core strength that must be continuously reinforced and enhanced. While strengthening ties with mature markets such as Europe and the United States and attracting international capital, Hong Kong would deepen co-operation with emerging markets in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Central Asia. It would open up two-way investment opportunities by bringing together capital and industries to meet development needs across these markets. Beyond promoting business and trade exchanges, Hong Kong would leverage its financial and professional services strengths, including green and sustainable finance and trade finance, to support infrastructure, supply chain and industrial development in the region, growing together with its regional partners. On offshore Renminbi business, Hong Kong is expanding its range of investment products, enhancing custody and collateral management infrastructure, and increasing liquidity to add depth and breadth to the market. Hong Kong would also develop gold storage, clearing and settlement services and related financial products, and explore closer connectivity with the Mainland gold market. These efforts would build a more comprehensive gold trading ecosystem and offer international investors more choices. Mr Chan said that "one country, two systems" provides Hong Kong with an institutional advantage for its long-term development, while talent is a key driving force for its future growth. Hong Kong would remain free, open, diverse and inclusive, welcoming enterprises and talent from around the world to establish and pursue careers in the city, as well as young people to study here, and encouraging them to become part of its future. Hong Kong would continue to attract international talent, promote exchanges across regions and cultures, and further strengthen its role in connecting the Mainland with the world. Mr Chan also took part in a broadcast fireside chat hosted by the Atlantic Council, a US think tank. He outlined the latest developments in Hong Kong's financial markets and how its first five-year plan would advance I&T, promote the integrated development of education, technology, talent and industries in the Northern Metropolis, and deepen co-operation with other GBA cities in I&T industries. On digital assets, he said that Hong Kong embraces financial innovation with an open mind. With equal emphasis on regulation and development, Hong Kong would take a prudent and measured approach to developing areas such as digital asset exchanges and stablecoins to better serve the real economy. Mr Chan also met with the Managing Director and Chief Administrative Officer of the WBG, Mr Zhang Wencai, today. They exchanged views on the global and regional economic outlook and deepening co-operation between Hong Kong and the WBG. Mr Chan said that Hong Kong could combine its strengths in capital markets and professional services with the project experiences and networks of multilateral development institutions to channel more private market capital and philanthropic funding into infrastructure and sustainable development projects in the region. A range of financial instruments could also be used to enhance project financing and risk management. Mr Chan also met with the management of a major European digital bank to discuss fintech development, digital banking services and cross-boundary payments, and outlined opportunities in Hong Kong's financial markets. He welcomed the bank to establish a presence in Hong Kong and leverage the city's vibrant financial services ecosystem, well-established financial infrastructure, professional talent and international networks to explore innovative financial services and expand its regional business. In the evening, Mr Chan attended a dinner organised by the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Bangkok, where he met with senior executives of major Thai banks and other financial institutions. He shared the latest developments in Hong Kong's economy and financial services sector and explored opportunities to further strengthen financial co-operation between the two places. Mr Chan will continue his visit to Bangkok tomorrow morning (October 17) before departing for Hong Kong, arriving in the afternoon.

items.title: Maiden voyage of southbound yachts from Guangdong realises two-way navigation for Guangdong-Hong Kong individual yacht travel (with photos/video)
items.description: The maiden voyage ceremony of southbound yachts from Guangdong was held today (October 16), marking the official implementation of the scheme. The Acting Financial Secretary, Mr Michael Wong; the Secretary for Transport and Logistics, Ms Mable Chan; and the Director of Marine, Mr Wong Sai-fat, officiated at the ceremony to welcome five visiting yachts from Guangdong. In his speech at the ceremony, the Acting Financial Secretary, Mr Michael Wong, said that Hong Kong is actively developing into a yachting hub in Asia. He noted that the global yacht market has continued to grow in recent years, with the luxury yacht market in particular experiencing significant expansion. He added that the market value of the superyacht industry is projected to reach approximately $350 billion by 2032, representing a massive scale. He believed that Hong Kong has the potential, capability, and strength to secure a share of this market. He said that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is proactively implementing various measures to promote the yacht economy, including the three measures introduced by the Marine Department in June to facilitate yachts to visit Hong Kong. He also mentioned that The Festival of Connoisseurs, an international flagship exhibition focusing on superyachts and premium lifestyles, will be held in Hong Kong in early November. He added that the Government is fully committed to promoting the construction of four new yacht clubs at the airport, Lamma Island, Aberdeen, and Hung Hom respectively, which will provide a total of more than 1 100 berths and four highly attractive new clubhouse facilities. It is expected that these facilities will significantly enhance and improve Hong Kong's infrastructure and ecosystem in the yachting economy. Following the launch of northbound travel of yachts from Hong Kong in June this year, and the signing of the relevant work arrangements between Guangdong and Hong Kong in September to establish an institutionalised mechanism for cross-boundary individual yacht travel between Guangdong and Hong Kong, the Governments of the two places have further implemented the southbound travel of yachts from Guangdong, enabling yacht owners in Guangdong to handle cross-boundary procedures more conveniently, thereby promoting greater connectivity between the two places in cross-boundary navigation networks and the marine leisure industry. Under the framework of the southbound travel of yachts from Guangdong, all Guangdong-registered yachts that meet the requirements of a navigation range of up to 20 nautical miles offshore and a wave resistance capability of not less than 2 metres may apply to visit Hong Kong. Yacht owners/masters intending to travel southbound may complete the procedures online in advance and must complete the relevant Chinese Mainland departure inspection formalities at the six designated control points (namely the Nansha Ferry Terminal in Guangzhou, Shekou Cruise Homeport in Shenzhen, Shenzhen Airport Ferry Terminal, Jiuzhou Port Passenger Terminal in Zhuhai, Wanshan Port in Zhuhai, and Sunsea Yacht Club Marina, Zhongshan Port). The Marine Department launched three facilitation measures in June, which include enhancing the Electronic Business System to allow one-stop online completion of arrival and port formalities, setting up designated anchorage areas and relaxing the requirements of booking a berth at a yacht club before arriving in Hong Kong, as well as authorising Chinese Mainland institutions to conduct the Hong Kong Waters Local Knowledge Examination and provide training for yacht masters prior to arrival in Hong Kong. These facilitation measures also apply to overseas yachts. Owners/masters of visiting yachts may apply through the Electronic Business System for Permission to Navigate in Hong Kong Waters as early as 30 days before arrival, and book an anchoring location. Details of the procedures and relevant information for Guangdong-registered yachts travelling southbound to Hong Kong are set out in the Appendix. The Marine Department has authorised two Mainland examination centres to conduct the Hong Kong Waters Local Knowledge Examination, and has approved seven Mainland training institutions to offer recognised training courses. To date, the department received an enthusiastic response with nearly 300 people having already obtained the relevant qualification. The Marine Department will also recognise online short-term training courses organised by local professional training and examination institutions in order to facilitate masters of visiting yachts in obtaining the qualification to navigate in Hong Kong waters while overseas. The implementation of the southbound travel of yachts from Guangdong and the relevant cross-boundary facilitation measures for yachts will help attract more yachts from the Greater Bay Area and around the world to visit Hong Kong, injecting new impetus into the tourism industry and the yacht market, bringing new growth opportunities and driving the development of related industries. The Government will continue to monitor the development of visiting yachts and make timely adjustments to the implementation of the various facilitation measures.

precise risk assessments: carrying out intensive and targeted mosquito control work at locations with more serious mosquito infestations, including stepping up inspections, eliminating mosquito breeding and potential breeding grounds, applying larvicides, conducting fogging operations to eradicate adult mosquitoes, and placing mosquito trapping devices at appropriate locations; promotion and education: organising exhibitions with relevant departments and stakeholders, and distributing leaflets and posters to enhance public awareness of mosquito control and prevention; and rapid alert mechanism: notifying residential estates that have subscribed to the gravidtrap Rapid Alert System, and advising property management companies and residents to stay vigilant and work together in taking mosquito prevention and elimination measures. ​During the follow-up actions and following the discovery of stagnant water at a private housing estate in Sha Tin District, the FEHD has issued a statutory notice to the responsible person-in-charge, requiring the clearance of such stagnant water within a specified timeframe. Public participation is crucial to the effective control of mosquito problems. The FEHD appeals to members of the public to continue to work together in strengthening personal mosquito control measures, including: tidying up their premises and checking for any accumulation of water inside the premises; removing all unnecessary water collections and eliminating the sources; checking household items (those placed in outdoor and open areas in particular), such as refuse containers, vases, air conditioner drip trays, and laundry racks to prevent stagnant water; changing water in flower vases and scrubbing their inner surfaces thoroughly, and removing water in saucers under potted plants at least once a week; properly covering all containers that hold water to prevent mosquitoes from accessing the water; properly disposing of articles that can contain water, such as disposable meal boxes and empty cans; and scrubbing drains and surface sewers with alkaline detergent at least once a week to remove any mosquito eggs. Starting in August 2025, following the completion of the surveillance of individual survey areas, and once the latest gravidtrap index and the density index are available, the FEHD has been disseminating relevant information through press releases, its website and social media. It aims to allow members of the public to quickly grasp the mosquito infestation situation and strengthen mosquito control efforts, thereby reducing the risk of chikungunya fever (CF) transmission. ​Following recommendations from the World Health Organization and taking into account the local situation in Hong Kong, the FEHD sets up gravidtraps in districts where mosquito-borne diseases have been recorded in the past, as well as in densely populated places such as housing estates, hospitals and schools to monitor the breeding and distribution of Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, which can transmit CF and dengue fever. At present, the FEHD has set up gravidtraps in 62 survey areas of the community, with a surveillance period of two weeks. During the surveillance period, the FEHD will collect the gravidtraps once a week. After the first week of surveillance, the FEHD will immediately examine the glue boards inside the retrieved gravidtraps for the presence of adult Aedine mosquitoes to compile the Gravidtrap Index (First Phase) and Density Index (First Phase). At the end of the second week of surveillance, the FEHD will instantly check the glue boards for the presence of adult Aedine mosquitoes. Data from the two weeks of surveillance will be combined to obtain the Area Gravidtrap Index and the Area Density Index. The Gravidtrap and Density indexes for Aedes albopictus in different survey areas, as well as information on mosquito prevention and control measures, are available on the department's webpage ( www.fehd.gov.hk/english/pestcontrol/dengue_fever/Dengue_Fever_Gravidtrap_Index_Update.html# ).

items.title: Remarks by STL at media session
items.description: Following are the remarks by the Secretary for Transport and Logistics, Ms Mable Chan, at a media session following the maiden voyage ceremony for the southbound travel of yachts from Guangdong today (October 16): Reporter: Given that there are only 150 berths at five anchorages, are you worried about running out of space during peak seasons? Under what circumstances will the Government consider capping daily visits and setting up more berth spots in the future? Secretary for Transport and Logistics: Having regard to the potential demand and the existing supply of mooring facilities in Hong Kong, we consider that there are adequate facilities for the mooring and docking of Mainland yachts to Hong Kong. At the present moment, we have allowed these Mainland yachts to dock or moor at five designated mooring anchorage areas, in addition to the existing mooring facilities in yacht clubs. We consider that this could meet the demand. Coupled with the real-time dynamic monitoring system, the Marine Department can communicate with the Mainland yacht captains so as to facilitate their travel in Hong Kong waters. We are also planning ahead. The Airport Authority Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government are planning for the development of four major new yacht parking facilities in different parts of Hong Kong, including the Airport island, Aberdeen, Lamma Island, and Hung Hom waterfront. We are working steadfastly on that. The Airport Authority Hong Kong is actually moving fast in inviting expressions of interest for the Yacht Bay on the Airport island. We expect they will invite tenders next year. (Please also refer to the Chinese portion of the remarks.)

items.title: Eight pieces of subsidiary legislation gazetted today to implement title registration system on new land
items.description: The Development Bureau (DEVB) gazetted eight pieces of subsidiary legislation today (October 16), proposing to make four new pieces of subsidiary legislation under the Land Titles Ordinance (Cap. 585) (LTO), and to amend four pieces of subsidiary legislation under the Land Registration Ordinance (Cap. 128) (LRO), the High Court Ordinance (Cap. 4) and the District Court Ordinance (Cap. 336), with a view to setting out implementation details for the title registration system to be implemented on new land in the first half of next year, and aligning certain practices under the current deeds registration system with the title registration system. A spokesperson for the DEVB said, "The Registration of Titles and Land (Miscellaneous Amendments) Ordinance 2025 was passed by the Legislative Council (LegCo) in September last year to amend the LTO, which was enacted in 2004 but has not yet come into operation, so as to implement the title registration system on new land first. To facilitate the implementation of the title registration system in the first half of next year, the DEVB and the Land Registry (LR) immediately commenced preparatory work to implement the new system, including the drafting of relevant subsidiary legislation. Once the new legislation comes into operation, new land will be registered under the new system, whilst existing land under the LRO will continue to be governed by the current deeds registration system until it is converted to the title registration system." "New land" refers to land held under a government lease granted on or after the date on which the amended Title Ordinance comes into operation. Generally speaking, this will include land granted on or after the operation date by way of land sale, by private treaty grant, and by land exchange. The eight pieces of subsidiary legislation gazetted set out the operational details for the title registration system, including the requirements and procedures for applications for registration, and operational matters relating to the processing of the applications by the LR; the management of the Land Titles Indemnity Fund and the procedures for claiming indemnity; new fee items; the introduction of arrangements such as electronic applications under the current deeds registration system, bringing it in line with the title registration system; and matters relating to proceedings to be brought before the Court. These eight pieces of subsidiary legislation comprise: Land Titles Regulation; Land Titles Indemnity Regulation; Land Titles (Fees and Levies) Regulation; Land Titles (Determination of Indemnity Cap) Notice; Land Registration (Amendment) Regulation 2026; Land Registration Fees (Amendment) Regulation 2026; Rules of the High Court (Amendment) Rules 2026; and Rules of the District Court (Amendment) Rules 2026. The spokesperson added, "Hong Kong is among the few economies that still run a deeds registration system. The implementation of the title registration system on new land will provide certainty in land ownership and simplify property transfer procedures, including eliminating the need to verify documents to confirm title during property transactions and the requirement to keep title deeds for many years. This will benefit the public and the business community, whilst bringing Hong Kong’s land registration system in line with other jurisdictions. The LR will continue to carry out publicity and education campaigns to ensure that the public and industry practitioners understand the detailed implementation arrangements under the new system." The eight pieces of subsidiary legislation will be tabled at the LegCo next Wednesday (October 21) for negative vetting. Upon passage, certain provisions relating to electronic applications under the Land Registration (Amendment) Regulation 2026 and the Land Registration Fees (Amendment) Regulation 2026 will come into force on October 4, 2027, in tandem with the e-lodgement system. The amended LTO and other subsidiary legislation will come into operation on a date to be specified separately by the Secretary for Development in the first half of 2027.

items.title: Hong Kong Customs detects two drug trafficking cases involving incoming passengers at airport (with photos)
items.description: ​Hong Kong Customs today (October 16) detected two drug trafficking cases at Hong Kong International Airport and seized about 8.8 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds and 220 duty-not-paid cigarettes, with a total estimated market value of about $1.83 million. In the first case, during an anti-narcotics operation conducted at Hong Kong International Airport today, Customs officers intercepted a 43-year-old Mainland female passenger and found about 3.3 kg of suspected cannabis buds and 220 duty-not-paid cigarettes inside her carry-on baggage. She was subsequently arrested. In the second case, a 41-year-old Mainland male passenger arrived in Hong Kong from Bangkok, Thailand, yesterday (October 15). During customs clearance, Customs officers found about 5.5 kg of suspected cannabis buds inside his carry-on baggage. He was subsequently arrested. The arrested woman in the first case has been charged with one count of trafficking in a dangerous drug and one count of possession of dutiable goods. The arrested man in the second case has been charged with one count of trafficking in a dangerous drug. The two cases will be brought up at the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts tomorrow (October 17). Customs will continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking activities through intelligence analysis. The department also reminds members of the public to stay alert and not participate in drug trafficking activities for monetary return. They must not accept hiring or delegation from another party to carry controlled items into and out of Hong Kong. They are also reminded not to carry unknown items for other people. Customs will continue to apply a risk assessment approach and focus on selecting passengers from high-risk regions for clearance to combat transnational drug trafficking activities. Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $5 million and life imprisonment. Under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance, cigarettes are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who imports, deals with, possesses, sells or buys illicit cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. Members of the public may report any suspected drug trafficking activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form ( eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: 15 persons arrested during anti-illegal worker operations
items.description: The Immigration Department (ImmD) mounted a series of territory-wide anti-illegal worker operations codenamed "Twilight", a joint operation with the Labour Department codenamed "Rainbow", joint operations with the Hong Kong Police Force (HKPF) codenamed "Champion", a joint operation with the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) and the Leisure and Cultural Services Department (LCSD) codenamed "Flabbergast", a joint operation with the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, and a joint operation with Hong Kong Customs, the HKPF, the FEHD and the LCSD from October 9 to yesterday (October 15). During the anti-illegal worker operations, ImmD officers raided multiple target locations including restaurants, retail stores and industrial buildings, etc. Twelve suspected illegal workers, one suspected employer, one suspected aider and abettor and one overstayer were arrested. The arrested suspected illegal workers comprised eight men and four women, aged 20 to 54. Among them, one man was holding a recognisance form which prohibits him from taking any employment. One woman aged 47 was suspected of employing the illegal workers and was arrested. The suspected aider and abettor arrested was a woman aged 28. Furthermore, the arrested overstayer was a man aged 43. An investigation into the suspected employer is ongoing, and the possibility of further arrests is not ruled out. An ImmD spokesman said, "Any person who contravenes a condition of stay in force in respect of him or her shall be guilty of an offence. Also, visitors are not allowed to take employment in Hong Kong, whether paid or unpaid, without the permission of the Director of Immigration. Offenders are liable to prosecution and upon conviction face a maximum fine of $50,000 and up to two years' imprisonment. Aiders and abettors are also liable to prosecution and penalties." The spokesman warned, "As stipulated in section 38AA of the Immigration Ordinance, an illegal immigrant, a person who is the subject of a removal order or a deportation order, an overstayer or a person who was refused permission to land is prohibited from taking any employment, whether paid or unpaid, or establishing or joining any business. Offenders are liable upon conviction to a maximum fine of $50,000 and up to three years' imprisonment. As stipulated in section 20(1)(a) of the Immigration Ordinance, the Chief Executive may make a deportation order against an immigrant, prohibiting the immigrant from being in Hong Kong at any time thereafter if the immigrant has been found guilty in Hong Kong of an offence punishable by imprisonment for not less than two years." The spokesman stressed that it is a serious offence to employ people who are not lawfully employable. Under the Immigration Ordinance, the maximum penalty for an employer employing a person who is not lawfully employable, i.e. an illegal immigrant, a person who is the subject of a removal order or a deportation order, an overstayer or a person who was refused permission to land, has been significantly increased from a fine of $350,000 and three years' imprisonment to a fine of $500,000 and 10 years' imprisonment to reflect the gravity of such offences. The director, manager, secretary, partner, etc, of the company concerned may also bear criminal liability. The High Court has laid down sentencing guidelines that the employer of an illegal worker should be given an immediate custodial sentence. According to the court sentencing, employers must take all practicable steps to determine whether a person is lawfully employable prior to employment. Apart from inspecting a prospective employee's identity card, the employer has the explicit duty to make enquiries regarding the person and ensure that the answers would not cast any reasonable doubt concerning the lawful employability of the person. The court will not accept failure to do so as a defence in proceedings. It is also an offence if an employer fails to inspect the job seeker's valid travel document if the job seeker does not have a Hong Kong permanent identity card. Offenders are liable upon conviction to a maximum fine of $150,000 and to imprisonment for one year. In that connection, the spokesman would like to remind all employers not to defy the law by employing illegal workers. The ImmD will continue to take resolute enforcement action to combat such offences. Under the existing mechanism, the ImmD will, as a standard procedure, conduct an initial screening of vulnerable persons, including illegal workers, illegal immigrants, sex workers and foreign domestic helpers, who are arrested during any operation with a view to ascertaining whether they are trafficking in persons (TIP) and/or forced labour victims. When any TIP and/or forced labour indicator is revealed in the initial screening, the ImmD officers will conduct a full debriefing and identification by using a standardised checklist to ascertain the presence of TIP and/or forced labour elements. Identified TIP and/or forced labour victims will be provided with various forms of support and assistance, including urgent intervention, medical services, counselling, shelter or temporary accommodation and other supporting services. The ImmD calls on TIP and/or forced labour victims to report crimes to the relevant departments immediately. For reporting illegal employment activities, please call the dedicated hotline 185 185, fax at 2824 1166, email anti_crime@immd.gov.hk , or submit the "Online Reporting of Immigration Offences" form at www.immd.gov.hk .

items.title: CHP announces new melioidosis case
items.description: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (October 16) announced that one new melioidosis case was recorded in the past week (October 9 to 15). The CHP appealed to members of the public to maintain personal and environmental hygiene to prevent melioidosis. The CHP also specifically reminded high-risk groups, including the elderly and people with underlying diseases, to avoid contact with soil or muddy water after typhoons or storms with a view to lowering infection risk. The case involves a 74-year-old female with underlying illnesses who lived in Sham Shui Po District. On October 4, she presented with a fever and cough with sputum. On October 7, she attended the Accident and Emergency Department of Caritas Medical Centre due to shortness of breath and was admitted for treatment on the same day. Her clinical diagnosis was pneumonia. Her clinical sample tested positive for Burkholderia pseudomallei. The patient passed away on October 8 and the cause of death is under investigation. The CHP is investigating the infection source of the case. An initial epidemiological investigation revealed that the case is sporadic. No epidemiological linkages have been established between this case and other confirmed cases previously recorded in Hong Kong. Person-to-person transmission and animal-to-human transmission are rare, but the bacteria causing melioidosis can survive in the local environment. Melioidosis is an endemic disease in Hong Kong, and melioidosis cases have been recorded in Hong Kong each year. As of yesterday (October 15), nine melioidosis cases have been recorded in Hong Kong this year. Last year, 21 melioidosis cases were recorded. According to literature, melioidosis cases are more common after typhoons or rainstorms. The bacterium Burkholderia pseudomallei in soil and muddy water may become exposed on the ground after typhoons or rainstorms, and the bacteria could spread more easily with strong winds or rainstorms. As such, the number of melioidosis cases may increase. Where practicable, members of the public should stay indoors during typhoons and rainstorms, avoid travelling to areas with potential flooding, and not wade in or have contact with muddy water and soil. In addition, high-risk individuals should avoid paths near stormwater drains where aerosols may be generated from contaminated water. Members of the public should also take the following preventive measures against infection: Avoid contact with contaminated soil; Wear appropriate protective clothing or footwear when participating in activities with possible contact with soil or water, e.g. using gloves and wearing boots. High-risk individuals may also consider wearing a surgical mask; Wash or shower after exposure to contaminated water or soil; Always clean any wounds as soon as possible and cover them with waterproof dressings; Wash hands with liquid soap and water after handling soil or gardening; Observe food hygiene and avoid drinking raw water; and Travellers can contract the disease through outdoor water sports. Risk of infection can be minimised by avoiding exposure to water sources (such as rivers, ponds or lakes) that might be contaminated. ​​The CHP appealed to members of the public to seek medical advice if they develop symptoms, in particular people with diabetes or other immunocompromising conditions, in order to receive an appropriate medical diagnosis and treatment. For more information on melioidosis, please visit the website of the CHP at www.chp.gov.hk/en/healthtopics/content/24/101110.html .

items.title: Speech by DSJ at graduation ceremony of Legal Practical Training Course for Chinese Enterprises Going Overseas (English only) (with photos)
items.description: Following is the speech by the Deputy Secretary for Justice, Dr Cheung Kwok-kwan, at the graduation ceremony of the Legal Practical Training Course for Chinese Enterprises Going Overseas today (October 16): Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, Good afternoon. I am delighted to address you all today as we mark the successful conclusion of the Legal Practical Training Course for Chinese Enterprises Going Overseas. On behalf of the Academy (Hong Kong International Legal Talents Training Academy), I extend my heartfelt congratulations and appreciation to all of you who have contributed to the success of this course. I would like to express our most sincere gratitude to 國資委 (State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council) for their unwavering support throughout the course. Our thanks also extend to our institutional partners and esteemed moderators and speakers who have played a pivotal role in enriching every aspect of this course. Since its launch in November 2024, the Academy has already partnered with around 30 international organisations and professional bodies to deliver capacity-building programmes for over 5 000 participants worldwide, covering topics including international law, Hong Kong common law, international arbitration and Chinese Mainland law, contributing to the cultivation of foreign-related legal talent. Over the last week of insightful lectures and lively exchange sessions covering common law, export control and sanctions, and international commercial and investment arbitration, I hope you have not only gained fresh perspectives that will advance your professional careers, but also acquired a deeper and first-hand understanding of Hong Kong's robust legal system and vibrant legal sector, and enjoyed a rewarding and fulfilling stay. Hong Kong's legal and professional services stand ready to support Chinese Mainland enterprises in their global expansion. In last year's edition of the course, we explored the opportunities in the markets of Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa. This year, we have turned our attention to the dynamic developments in Central Asia and Latin America. Together, we now have a more complete picture of the challenges faced by Chinese Mainland enterprises going global. In June this year, I had the privilege of joining a highly fruitful delegation led by the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. The visit demonstrated that Hong Kong is a trusted partner not only to these emerging markets, but also to Chinese Mainland enterprises seeking to expand into these markets and beyond. Hong Kong is an international financial centre and international trade centre connecting global capital to the Chinese Mainland. As an international legal hub, Hong Kong can bring you a robust common law system, a deep pool of seasoned professionals with extensive international networks, and a transparent and sound regulatory framework. We offer certainty, predictability and effectiveness essential to cross-border dispute resolution. On a related note, I am pleased to highlight several key initiatives launched by our Department (Department of Justice), this year, some of which may already have been discussed during the final panel discussion of the course just now. These include the publication of the Panel List of Hong Kong Legal Service Providers Supporting "Go Global", comprising over 70 legal services providers in Hong Kong to facilitate precise connections of Chinese Mainland enterprises with Hong Kong's legal professional services based on their specific needs for expanding overseas. Moreover, our Department has published two collections of success stories ("Collection of Success Stories: Hong Kong's Professional Services Supporting Chinese Mainland Enterprises Going Global"), featuring over 200 success stories. Covering various professional fields, including legal, financial, accounting and business consultancy services, as well as different industries and investment destinations, the case studies use real-life examples to demonstrate the value contributed by Hong Kong's professional services throughout the entire business cycle of internationalisation. Our professional services can offer comprehensive support, safeguard corporate interests and mitigate operational risks. I encourage you to bring in Hong Kong professional services early in the planning stage of your company's overseas expansion to minimise risks. As we wrap up this course, I invite each of you to take a few minutes to complete the feedback form and tell us how we can improve our training courses in future. Last but not least, I warmly invite you to join our Hong Kong Legal Week 2026, which will be held in Hong Kong from November 2 to 6 this year. As our annual flagship event, Hong Kong Legal Week brings together legal professionals, business leaders, policymakers, academics and representatives from leading international organisations from Hong Kong and around the world. This year's theme, "Collaboration & Innovation: Legal Synergy for a Shared Future", will feature practical exchanges and forward-looking discussions on cross-border trade, international legal co-operation, lawtech, and development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and beyond. Please feel free to register in person or online at our website. Ladies and gentlemen, congratulations once again. I wish you every success in your future endeavours, and a safe and pleasant journey home. Thank you very much.

items.title: Update on mosquito-borne diseases, dengue fever and chikungunya fever
items.description: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (October 16) announced the latest situation regarding dengue fever (DF) and chikungunya fever (CF). Although Hong Kong has entered autumn, the weather has yet to cool down and there are occasional showers, which is favourable for mosquito breeding. Members of the public are reminded to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and mosquito breeding, both in Hong Kong and when travelling to areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. Dengue fever ---------------- From October 9 to yesterday (October 15), the CHP recorded one imported DF case. The patient had visited Cambodia during the incubation period. Hong Kong has recorded 34 DF cases so far this year, comprising 32 imported cases and two local cases. A total of 59 DF cases were recorded last year (2025), all of which were imported cases. In 2024, 161 DF cases were recorded, comprising 156 imported cases and five local cases. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the global incidence of DF has markedly increased over the past two decades, posing a substantial public health challenge. In 2024, the WHO recorded over 14 million DF cases, which was a record number. In 2025, over five million cases and over 4 000 DF-related deaths were reported in over 90 countries/territories. From January to August 2026, around 2.2 million cases and over 1 100 DF-related deaths have been recorded globally. DF has long been prevalent in many neighbouring tourist destinations. So far this year, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Sri Lanka and Vietnam each recorded over 100 000 cases; Indonesia recorded over 80 000 cases; Malaysia recorded over 70 000 cases; and Singapore recorded over 2 600 cases. Meanwhile, according to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, as of September, Guangdong Province has recorded 586 cases this year, of which 155 were recorded in September alone. Detailed information on the latest DF situation in Hong Kong, as well as neighbouring and overseas countries and areas, has been uploaded to the CHP's website . Chikungunya fever ----------------------- From October 9 to yesterday, the CHP recorded two imported CF cases, involving two males, aged 17 and 64 respectively. Both patients had visited the Chinese Mainland during the incubation period. The CHP considers that both patients were infected during travel. Both cases were classified as imported. They were admitted to hospital for treatment in a mosquito-free environment. The 17-year-old patient has recovered and been discharged, while the 64-year-old patient is currently in stable condition. The CHP's epidemiological investigation is ongoing. Both cases have been reported to the Chinese Mainland health authority. Hong Kong has recorded seven confirmed CF cases so far this year, including six imported cases and one local case. Hong Kong recorded a total of 82 confirmed CF cases last year. Among them, 11 were local cases and the rest were imported cases. According to the WHO, a total of 502 264 CF cases and 186 CF-related deaths were reported in 41 countries/territories last year. Cases were reported in the Americas, Africa, Asia and Europe. According to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, Guangdong Province has recorded 1 753 cases this year (as of September). Among them, 1 014 were recorded in September, a sharp increase compared to the number of cases recorded from June to August (36 to 496 cases). Preventive measures to be taken by the public ---------------------------------------------------- The CHP reminds members of the public to maintain good environmental hygiene, and to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and mosquito breeding, both in Hong Kong and when travelling to areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. Mosquito-borne diseases such as DF and CF are endemic in various countries worldwide. The risk of importation persists. Members of the public should check the situation at their destinations before travelling abroad, especially when travelling to Southeast Asian countries. Additionally, whether travelling or not, members of the public should use DEET-containing insect repellents or other effective active ingredients properly to prevent mosquito bites, but the following precautions should be taken when using them: read the label instructions carefully first; apply right before entering an area with a risk of mosquito bites; apply on exposed skin and clothing; use DEET of up to 30 per cent for pregnant women and up to 10 per cent for children (for children who travel to countries or areas where mosquito-borne diseases are endemic or epidemic, and where exposure is likely, those aged 2 months or above can use DEET-containing insect repellents with a DEET concentration of up to 30 per cent); apply sunscreen first, then insect repellent; reapply only when needed and follow the instructions; and in addition to DEET, there are other insect repellents available on the market containing different active ingredients, such as IR3535 and picaridin. When using any insect repellent, the public should follow the usage instructions and precautions on the product label. ​The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) appeals to members of the public to continue to stay alert and work together to carry out mosquito prevention and control measures early, including inspecting their homes and surroundings to remove potential breeding grounds, changing water in vases and scrubbing their inner surfaces, removing water in saucers under potted plants at least once a week, and properly disposing of containers such as empty cans and lunch boxes. The FEHD also advises members of the public and property management agencies to keep drains free of blockage and level all defective ground surfaces to prevent the accumulation of water. They should also scrub all drains and surface sewers with an alkaline detergent at least once a week to remove any mosquito eggs. ​The public should call 1823 in case of mosquito problems, and may visit the following pages for more information: the CF page of the CHP and the Travel Health Service , the latest Travel Health News , tips for using insect repellents , and the CHP Facebook Page , Instagram Account and YouTube Channel , and also the Mosquito Prevention and Control dedicated page of the FEHD.

items.title: Woman sentenced to 10 months' imprisonment for smuggling dried shark fins (with photo)
items.description: A 29-year-old Chinese woman, who smuggled dried shark fins into Hong Kong, was convicted at the District Court today (October 16) for violating the Protection of Endangered Species of Animals and Plants Ordinance (Cap. 586) (the Ordinance) and sentenced to 10 months' imprisonment. A spokesman for the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) said that the passenger arrived at Hong Kong International Airport from Brazil via Ethiopia on March 22 this year. Upon inspection of her luggage by Customs officers, a batch of suspected scheduled dried shark fins was found inside the luggage. AFCD officers subsequently attended the scene, examined the specimens and confirmed that they were scheduled dried shark fins, weighing a total of about 52 kilograms, with an estimated market value of about $200,000. The woman was prosecuted by the AFCD for illegal import of specimens of endangered species. She was convicted at the District Court today, and the court adopted a starting point of 15 months' imprisonment for sentencing. With a one-third reduction given for her guilty plea, the defendant was sentenced to 10 months' imprisonment. Some shark and ray species are listed in the Appendices to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, and are regulated under the Ordinance in Hong Kong. Any person who imports, exports or possesses specimens of endangered species not in accordance with the Ordinance commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a maximum fine of $10 million and imprisonment for 10 years with the specimens forfeited. The spokesman said, "The Government is committed to protecting endangered species. The AFCD and Hong Kong Customs will remain vigilant and continue to monitor and combat illegal activities involving endangered species." Members of the public may call 1823 to report any suspected irregularities to the AFCD and visit the AFCD website at www.cites.hk for information on the control of endangered species in Hong Kong.

items.title: Light Public Housing enters new phase of circulation: applications now open for all projects (with photos)
items.description: The Housing Bureau (HB) today (October 16) announced that with the Light Public Housing (LPH) entering a new phase of circulation, all 13 LPH projects are open for application from today. With the last two LPH projects, namely the new projects converted from school premises at Shun Lee Tsuen Road, Kwun Tong, and Chuk Yuen Road, Wong Tai Sin (providing a total of about 210 units), set to be completed progressively in the first quarter of next year, all 13 LPH projects will then be fully completed. The other 11 projects are Yau Pok Road, Yuen Long; Choi Hing Road, Ngau Tau Kok; Choi Shek Lane, Kowloon Bay; Tsing Fuk Lane, Tuen Mun; Olympic Avenue, Kai Tak; Sheung On Street, Chai Wan; Yan Po Road, Tuen Mun; Tsing Fat Street, Tuen Mun; Hang Kwong Street, Ma On Shan; Shun On Road, Kwun Tong; and Choi Yuen Road, Sheung Shui. Eligible applicants will receive the application forms by post sent by the HB in batches starting today. Application forms submitted on or before November 6 will be handled with priority. Those who have submitted an application form previously do not need to reapply. As all LPH projects have now been launched, the HB will continue to keep all projects open for applications from eligible persons after November 6. About 30 000 units completed ahead of target; unit circulation benefits families in need A spokesman for the HB said, "Under the direction of the HB, all approximately 30 000 LPH units will be completed by the end of March next year, taking just over four years to accomplish, ahead of the five-year construction target set out in the 2022 Policy Address. Applications for LPH have received an overwhelming response since opening, with over 44 900 applications received as of late September. With full intake achieved at a number of projects, some residents have successfully moved into traditional public rental housing (PRH), resulting in turnover of units. These vacated units will then be allocated to other families with urgent housing needs. LPH offers affordable rent, comprehensive ancillary services and a better living environment, continuously providing sufficient housing options for families with urgent housing needs, including those residing in subdivided units (SDUs). Far superior to inadequate housing; apply early to improve living conditions The spokesman added, "The 13 projects are located across Hong Kong Island, Kowloon and the New Territories, each varying in scale and featuring its own merits. With all projects now open, we believe that they can well cater for the diverse needs of different applicants. More importantly, the living environment and ancillary facilities of all LPH projects are far superior to any inadequate housing, such as substandard SDUs. Eligible residents can also apply for the Trial Scheme on Special Allowance for Households of LPH funded by the Community Care Fund, which provides one-off special allowances ranging from $1,950 to $13,000. This allowance aims to alleviate the financial pressure of relocation and community adaption, such as children's school transfer, furniture and appliance purchase, and re-establishment of social networks. We estimate that the beneficiary residents will save over $7.55 billion in total expenditure over five years. The affordable rent of LPH will considerably alleviate the rental burden on grassroots families, enabling them to reallocate their savings towards other meaningful purposes. This will not only bring immediate improvements to their personal and family life, but also facilitate their long-term planning. In addition, subject to actual circumstances, project operators will actively provide a range of daily ancillary facilities, such as 24-hour self-service laundries, catering facilities, convenience stores, fresh provision shops, hair salons, study rooms and activity rooms. A variety of services and activities will also be provided, including community tours, employment counselling and assistance, school transfer support, child care services and homework guidance, mobile Chinese medicine clinics and festive events. These initiatives are designed to help residents seamlessly transition into the new environment and familiarise themselves with the neighbouring communities. We urge eligible members of the public in need to submit their applications as soon as possible." Application details Details of the LPH application are as follows: (1) Eligibility for priority application: General applicants for traditional PRH (i.e., families of two or more persons and elderly one-person applicants) who have been on the waiting list for three years or more will be given priority. Eligible persons will receive their application forms by post from the HB in batches. (2) Application period: Completed application forms submitted on or before November 6 will be processed with priority. (3) Continuous application: The HB will continue to keep all projects open for applications from eligible persons after November 6. (4) Submission methods: Interested applicants may return their completed application forms by post to the Dedicated Team on Light Public Housing of the Housing Bureau (P.O. Box 28222, Gloucester Road Post Office, Wan Chai, Hong Kong); or by depositing them into drop-in boxes during office hours (from 9am to 6pm, Mondays to Fridays, except Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays) at the following locations: • Light Public Housing Information Counter at Podium Level 2, Hong Kong Housing Authority Customer Service Centre, 3 Wang Tau Hom South Road, Kowloon • Office of the Dedicated Team on Light Public Housing at Room 801, 8/F, Revenue Tower, 5 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong Alternatively, if the applicant and all family members have registered for "iAM Smart+", they may choose to complete, sign and submit an electronic form by scanning the exclusive QR code pre-printed on the application form. The HB will process the application forms received and make arrangements for the allocation as soon as possible. To ensure families with greater need are prioritised, higher allocation priority will be given to applicants who are currently living in inadequate housing, have special medical conditions, or have family members who are minor children, newborn babies, elderly persons, etc. Information on the two new LPH projects is as follows: (1) Shun Lee Tsuen Road, Kwun Tong (converted from school premises): Providing about 110 units (including units for one to two persons and three to four persons), about a five-minute walk to Shun Tin Bus Terminus, which provides various franchised bus and minibus routes to/from Choi Hung MTR Station and different districts across Hong Kong and Kowloon. The estimated monthly rent ranges from about $1,390 to $2,670 (Note). (2) Chuk Yuen Road, Wong Tai Sin (converted from school premises): Providing about 100 units (including units for one to two persons, three to four persons and four to five persons), about a five-minute walk to the bus stop and minibus stop at Chuk Yuen Road, which provide various franchised bus and minibus routes to/from Wong Tai Sin MTR Station and different districts across Hong Kong and Kowloon. The estimated monthly rent ranges from about $1,470 to $3,330 (Note). For more information about the LPH application, including details of all 13 projects, please refer to the enclosed LPH promotional pamphlets, or visit the HB's LPH website ( www.hb.gov.hk/eng/lph ). For enquiries, please call 3464 0700, or email lphapp@hb.gov.hk . Note: Rents vary depending on the unit size and the district. The rental level is set at around 90 per cent of the rent of newly completed traditional PRH in the same district. items.title: Secretary for Health meets Director-General of Beijing Municipal Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (with photos)
items.description: The Secretary for Health, Professor Lo Chung-mau, led a delegation to meet with the Director-General of the Beijing Municipal Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Mr Luo Zenggang, in Beijing today (October 16) to introduce the policy directions and latest measures for the development of Chinese medicine (CM) in Hong Kong, and explore deepening the co-operation between Beijing and Hong Kong in the CM field on various fronts. Professor Lo said, "The National 15th Five-Year Plan proposes advancing the inheritance and innovation of CM and promoting CM to go global. The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Government actively dovetails with the national strategies to promote comprehensive, high-quality, and high-standard development of CM. The HKSAR Government, for the first time, has formulated the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) (Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan), comprehensively and proactively aligning with the National 15th Five-Year Plan. Interconnected with Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan, the 2026 Policy Address announced by the Chief Executive last month puts forward a number of specific policy measures to promote CM development. These include the launch of 24-hour in-patient services at The Chinese Medicine Hospital of Hong Kong (CMHHK) by the end of this year, the establishment of the International Consortium of Herb-Drug Interaction, the continued development of the Hospital Authority's integrated Chinese-Western Medicine services, and the sponsoring of regional and international CM conferences and exhibitions, signifying more breakthroughs and opportunities ahead for the development of CM in Hong Kong. At the same time, with the Chinese Medicine Development Blueprint as an anchor, Hong Kong will continue to advance the development of CM in an orderly manner and leverage the two flagship institutions, CMHHK and the Government Chinese Medicines Testing Institute, to further promote CM development in Hong Kong on all fronts." Professor Lo expressed his gratitude to the Beijing Municipal Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine for its continuous support for CM development in Hong Kong. He said he hoped that the two places would continue to deepen exchanges and collaboration in areas including CM policy measures, clinical services, talent cultivation, and the commercialisation of scientific and technological achievements, thereby promoting high-quality CM development in both places. The Director of Health, Dr Ronald Lam, and the Controller-designate for Medical Products Regulation, Mr Li Zili, also attended the meeting. Professor Lo will lead a delegation tomorrow (October 17) to attend the World Conference on Traditional Medicine 2026 to be held in Beijing for two consecutive days, and will return to Hong Kong in the afternoon of October 18.

items.title: Appointment of non-permanent judge from another common law jurisdiction of Court of Final Appeal
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Judiciary: Chief Justice Andrew Cheung, Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal, today (October 16) welcomed the acceptance by the Chief Executive of the recommendation of the Judicial Officers Recommendation Commission on the appointment of the Honourable Sir Terence Arnold as a non-permanent judge from another common law jurisdiction of the Court of Final Appeal. The Chief Justice noted that the Government would be seeking the endorsement of the Legislative Council of the recommended appointment. The Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal Ordinance (Cap. 484) provides for a list of non-permanent Hong Kong judges and a list of non-permanent judges from other common law jurisdictions. Currently, there are four non-permanent Hong Kong judges and five non-permanent judges from other common law jurisdictions. The maximum number of non-permanent judges is 30. In hearing and determining an appeal, the Court of Final Appeal is constituted by five judges, i.e. the Chief Justice, three permanent judges and one non-permanent Hong Kong judge or one non-permanent judge from another common law jurisdiction. The recommended appointment of Sir Terence Arnold to the Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal will increase the number of non-permanent judges from other common law jurisdictions from five to six. This will provide greater flexibility in dealing with the caseload of the Court of Final Appeal.

items.title: Reappointment of Non-Executive Directors to SFC announced
