items.title: Senior judicial appointment: non-permanent judge from another common law jurisdiction of the Court of Final Appeal
items.description: The Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, has accepted the recommendation of the Judicial Officers Recommendation Commission (JORC) on the appointment of the Honourable Sir Terence Arnold as a non-permanent judge from another common law jurisdiction of the Court of Final Appeal. Subject to the endorsement of the Legislative Council, the Chief Executive will make the appointment under Article 88 of the Basic Law and section 9 of the Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal Ordinance (Cap. 484). Mr Lee said, "I am pleased to accept the JORC's recommendation on the appointment of Sir Terence Arnold as a non-permanent judge from another common law jurisdiction of the Court of Final Appeal. Sir Terence Arnold retired from the judicial office of Permanent Judge of the Supreme Court of New Zealand, New Zealand's final court of appeal, in April 2017. He is a judge of eminent standing and reputation. I am confident that he will contribute substantively to the Court of Final Appeal. "With the appointment of Sir Terence Arnold, the list of non-permanent judges from other common law jurisdictions will consist of six eminent judges from the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand. The presence of these esteemed overseas jurists as non-permanent judges of the Court of Final Appeal is a manifestation of the independence of the Judiciary in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) as protected by the Basic Law. Their participation demonstrates a high degree of confidence in the HKSAR's judicial system, and enables Hong Kong to maintain strong links with other common law jurisdictions. I am fully confident that these distinguished jurists from overseas with profound judicial experience will remain as a unique strength of the HKSAR's judicial system." Article 90 of the Basic Law and section 7A of the Ordinance provide that the Chief Executive shall obtain the endorsement of the Legislative Council on the appointment of judges of the Court of Final Appeal. The Government will seek the endorsement of the Legislative Council of the recommended appointment in due course. The curriculum vitae of Sir Terence Arnold is at the Annex.

items.title: Inspection of aquatic products imported from Japan
items.description: In response to the Japanese Government's plan to discharge nuclear-contaminated water at the Fukushima Nuclear Power Station, the Director of Food and Environmental Hygiene issued a Food Safety Order which prohibits all aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds originating from the 10 metropolis/prefectures, namely Tokyo, Fukushima, Ibaraki, Miyagi, Chiba, Gunma, Tochigi, Niigata, Nagano and Saitama, from being imported into and supplied in Hong Kong. For other Japanese aquatic products, sea salt and seaweeds that are not prohibited from being imported into Hong Kong, the Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department is conducting comprehensive radiological tests to verify that the radiation levels of these products do not exceed the guideline levels before they are allowed to be supplied in the market. From noon on October 15 to noon today (October 16), the CFS conducted tests on the radiological levels of 204 food samples imported from Japan, which were of the "aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt" category. No sample was found to have exceeded the safety limit. Details can be found on the CFS's thematic website titled "Control Measures on Foods Imported from Japan" ( www.cfs.gov.hk/english/programme/programme_rafs/programme_rafs_fc_01_30_Nuclear_Event_and_Food_Safety.html ). In parallel, the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) has also tested 50 samples of local catch for radiological levels. All the samples passed the tests. Details can be found on the AFCD's website ( www.afcd.gov.hk/english/fisheries/Radiological_testing/Radiological_Test.html ). The Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) has also enhanced the environmental monitoring of the local waters. No anomaly has been detected so far. For details, please refer to the HKO's website ( www.hko.gov.hk/en/radiation/monitoring/seawater.html ). From August 24, 2023, to noon today, the CFS and the AFCD have conducted tests on the radiological levels of 268 278 samples of food imported from Japan (including 166 969 samples of aquatic and related products, seaweeds and sea salt) and 57 110 samples of local catch respectively. All the samples passed the tests.

items.title: SJ attends Hainan Legal Week to deepen co-operation in legal services between Hong Kong and Hainan (with photos)
items.description: The Secretary for Justice, Mr Paul Lam, SC, attended the 2026 Hainan Free Trade Port Legal Week (Hainan Legal Week) in Hainan today (October 16) to promote Hong Kong's advantage in professional services and deepen co-operation in legal and dispute resolution services between Hong Kong and Hainan, driving the two places to contribute to the high-quality development of the country by leveraging the synergy of "connection of the two ports". This year's Hainan Legal Week is themed "Law-based Free Trade Port‧ Connect with the World". Speaking at the opening ceremony, Mr Lam said that Hong Kong and Hainan have maintained close relationships with close personal ties and business connections. During the National 15th Five-Year Plan period, Hainan will strengthen the construction of foreign-related rule of law and position the Hainan Free Trade Port as a preferred destination for resolving international commercial disputes. Meanwhile, Hong Kong will deepen its development into an international legal and dispute resolution services centre, leverage its strengths in professional services to assist Mainland enterprises in going global, and develop into an international hub for the pooling of high-calibre talent. He stated that the talent pooled in Hong Kong can make the most of their strengths to serve Hainan's needs, supporting Hainan to optimise its business environment governed by the rule of law. Also, Hainan shoulders the national strategic role of developing commercial aerospace as a strategic emerging industry. Hong Kong can provide tailored legal and professional services to support the commercialisation of aerospace development. Mr Lam encouraged aerospace enterprises from Hainan and across the country to adopt Hong Kong law as the applicable law in their contracts and choose Hong Kong as a venue for diversified dispute resolution. During the ceremony, Mr Lam and the Director-General of the Department of Justice of Hainan Province, Mr Qiu Lijun, signed a co-operation arrangement in the area of legal services, with a view to deepening co-operation between the Department of Justice and the Department of Justice of Hainan Province, including promoting legal services co-operation, foreign-related legal talent training, and mutual exchanges between Hong Kong and Hainan. Mr Lam then attended an exchange session on advancing the implementation of the co-operation arrangement and met with leaders of the Department of Justice of Hainan Province and representatives of the Hainan Lawyers Association. Mr Lam will return to Hong Kong this evening.

items.title: Business expectations for fourth quarter of 2026
items.description: The Census and Statistics Department (C&SD) released today (October 16) the results of the Quarterly Business Tendency Survey for the fourth quarter (Q4) of 2026. Business Situation For all surveyed sectors taken together, the proportion of respondents expecting their business situation to be better (14%) in Q4 2026 over the preceding quarter is higher than that expecting it to be worse (9%). When compared with the results of the Q3 2026 survey round, the proportion of respondents expecting a better business situation in Q4 2026 is 14%, higher than the corresponding proportion of 10% in Q3 2026. On the other hand, the proportion of respondents expecting a worse business situation had decreased from 14% in Q3 2026 to 9% in Q4 2026. Analysed by sector, respondents in most of the surveyed sectors expect their business situation to increase on balance or remain broadly unchanged in Q4 2026 as compared with Q3 2026. In particular, more respondents in the accommodation and food services and financing and insurance sectors expect their business situation to be better in Q4 2026 as compared with Q3 2026. On the other hand, in the transportation, storage and courier services sector, more respondents expect their business situation to be worse, as compared to those expecting it to be better. The results of the survey should be interpreted with care. In this type of survey on expectations, the views collected in the survey are affected by the events in the community occurring around the time of enumeration, and it is difficult to establish precisely the extent to which respondents' perception of the future accords with the underlying trends. The enumeration period for this survey round was from September 1, 2026 to October 6, 2026. Volume of Business / Output Respondents in most surveyed sectors expect their volume of business/output to increase on balance or remain broadly unchanged in Q4 2026 as compared with Q3 2026. In particular, more respondents in the accommodation and food services, manufacturing, financing and insurance and retail sectors expect their volume of business/production/sales to increase in Q4 2026 over Q3 2026. Employment Respondents in a number of the surveyed sectors expect their employment to remain broadly unchanged in Q4 2026 as compared with Q3 2026. Nevertheless, more respondents in the accommodation and food services and real estate sectors expect their employment to increase in Q4 2026 over Q3 2026. On the other hand, more respondents in the information and communications and construction sectors expect their employment to decrease, as compared to those expecting it to increase. Selling Price / Service Charge Respondents in most of the surveyed sectors expect their selling prices/service charges to increase on balance or remain broadly unchanged in Q4 2026 as compared with Q3 2026. In particular, more respondents in the accommodation and food services and transportation, storage and courier services sectors expect their prices of food provided/charges for services rendered to go up in Q4 2026 over Q3 2026. However, more respondents in the construction sector expect their tender prices to go down in Q4 2026 over Q3 2026. Commentary A Government spokesman said that the overall near-term business outlook among large enterprises for the fourth quarter of 2026 strengthened notably, registering a net positive balance of enterprises that expected their business situation to improve over the previous quarter, the first time in ten quarters. Most sectors saw improvements in their outlook. The overall hiring appetite also improved slightly. Looking ahead, continued solid growth in the Hong Kong economy will render support to local business outlook. Nonetheless, uncertainties remain in the external environment, which may affect near-term sentiment. The Government will continue to closely monitor the situation. Further Information The survey gathers views on short-term business performance from the senior management of about 570 prominent companies in various sectors in Hong Kong with a view to providing a quick reference, with minimum time lag, for predicting the short-term future economic performance of the local economy. The survey covers 10 major sectors in Hong Kong, namely manufacturing; construction; import / export trade and wholesale; retail; accommodation and food services (mainly covering services rendered by hotels and restaurants); transportation, storage and courier services; information and communications; financing and insurance; real estate; and professional and business services sectors. Views collected in the survey refer only to those of respondents on their own companies rather than those on the respective sectors they are engaged in, and are limited to the expected direction of quarter-to-quarter change (e.g. "up", "same" or "down") but not the magnitude of change. In collecting views on the quarter-to-quarter changes, if the variable in question is subject to seasonal variations, respondents are asked to provide the expected changes after excluding the normal seasonal variations. Survey results are generally presented as "net balance", i.e. the difference between the percentage of respondents choosing "up" and that choosing "down". The percentage distribution of respondents among various response categories (e.g. "up", "same" and "down") reflects how varied their business expectations are. The "net balance", with its appropriate sign, indicates the direction of expected change in the variable concerned. A positive sign indicates a likely upward trend while a negative sign indicates a likely downward trend. However, the magnitude of the "net balance" reflects only the prevalence of optimism or pessimism, but not the magnitude of expected change, since information relating to such magnitude is not collected in the survey. Furthermore, owing to sample size constraint, care should be taken in interpreting survey results involving a small percentage (e.g. less than 10%) of respondents in individual sectors. Chart 1 shows the views on expected changes in business situation for the period Q4 2025 to Q4 2026. Table 1 shows the net balances of views on expectations in respect of different variables for Q4 2026. The survey results are published in greater detail in the "Report on Quarterly Business Tendency Survey, Q4 2026". Users can browse and download the publication at the website of the C&SD ( www.censtatd.gov.hk/en/EIndexbySubject.html?pcode=B1110008&scode=300 ). ​ Users who have enquiries about the survey results may contact the Business Expectation Statistics Section of the C&SD (Tel: 3903 7263; E-mail: business-prospects@censtatd.gov.hk ).

items.title: Auction for Che Kung Festival Fair stalls to be held on October 30
items.description: ​The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) announced today (October 16) that stalls at the 2027 Che Kung Festival (CKF) Fair will be put up for open auction on October 30 (Friday). A spokesman for the FEHD said that the annual CKF Fair will be held for 18 consecutive days from February 3 to 20, 2027, at Chui Tin Street Soccer Pitch in Sha Tin. A total of 48 dry goods stalls will be put up for auction, with an upset price of $2,770. The open auction will be held at the Assembly Hall, 2/F, Lai Chi Kok Government Offices, 19 Lai Wan Road, Lai Chi Kok, Kowloon, on October 30 starting from 9am until the completion of the auction. Bidders for the CKF Fair stalls must be at least 18 years old and ordinarily reside in Hong Kong. Bidders can bid for more than one stall. A bidder must pay the bid price and register in person with his/her own name as the licensee of the stall immediately after successfully bidding for a stall. The bidder is also required to sign at once a licence agreement with the FEHD; otherwise, he/she will forfeit the rights to operate the stall. The CKF Fair site will be made available to the licensees two days in advance of the fair (February 1 and 2, 2027) for the setting up of stalls. In the event of any unforeseeable incident that will cause a reduction of the whole licence period (including the duration for setting up stalls and the business period of the fair), the Government has the right to postpone the commencement date and shorten the duration of the period. The bidding price (licence fee) paid will be refunded to the successful bidder on a pro-rata basis without interest. The FEHD reminds licensees that the stalls are solely for the purpose of selling and promoting the sale of the permitted commodities, and no other activities are allowed in the licensed area. If the FEHD considers that any activity conducted by the licensee to publicise, promote, display, show, sell or gift any permitted commodities in the venue is unlawful, contrary to the interest of national security, immoral or incompatible with the object of the CKF Fair, the FEHD is entitled to direct the licensee to stop conducting such activity and the licensee must immediately comply with such direction. Stall licensees must not destroy, damage or abandon any unsold commodities at or in the vicinity of the stall. They must completely remove the stall structure and all paraphernalia, together with all refuse, debris and unsold commodities (whether damaged or otherwise), from the licensed area before 10pm on February 20, 2027. According to the licence agreement, licensees must not keep, store or use any compressed helium cylinders in the licenced area. Sales of floating LED glowing balloons and aquarium fish by stall licensees are prohibited at the CKF Fair. In addition, as stated in the licence agreement, the height of dry goods stalls must not exceed 3 metres from ground level. Also, each corner and anchor point of the marquee (if any) shall be securely fastened using appropriate ballast weights, such as sandbags or purpose-designed marquee water weights. During the period when the Strong Monsoon Signal is in force or is to be issued, the licensee shall immediately inspect the stall and adopt reinforcement measures as necessary. Successful bidders shall comply with all the stipulations and provisions as set out in the licence agreement. Otherwise, the department is entitled to terminate the agreement and the licensee shall immediately vacate the stall. Details of the 2027 CKF Fair, such as the public notice, the location and layout of the fair venue, commodities allowed for sale at the fair stalls, open auction arrangements and related rules, as well as a sample of the licence agreement, are available on the FEHD website ( www.fehd.gov.hk ). Interested bidders may visit the website or contact the FEHD's Sha Tin District Environmental Hygiene Office (2634 0134) for enquires.

items.title: TD urges public and visitors to plan cross-boundary trips early before and after Chung Yeung Festival holiday
items.description: The Transport Department (TD) today (October 16) said that the passenger and vehicle traffic at land boundary control points (BCPs) will significantly increase before and after the Chung Yeung Festival holiday (October 16 to 19), especially amid the expected inbound peak on Monday (October 19) afternoon and evening when waiting times for public transport (PT) services will be longer. Cross-boundary travellers are urged to plan their trips early and properly, allow sufficient travelling time, avoid travelling during peak hours as far as possible and heed the latest traffic and PT information of BCPs. Enhancing services for travel convenience The TD has been steering local and cross-boundary public transport operators (PTOs) to strengthen their services before and after the Chung Yeung Festival holiday for the convenience of residents and visitors, including: The MTR Corporation Limited will enhance the train services of the East Rail Line between Admiralty and Lo Wu/Lok Ma Chau Stations at different times from October 16 to 19 based on passenger demand; The Hong Kong Section of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link will operate additional short-haul trips between Hong Kong West Kowloon Station and Futian and Shenzhenbei Stations (see details at the 12306.cn website); The frequency of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge (HZMB) shuttle bus (Gold Bus) will be increased to an average of about one minute during peak hours; The cross-boundary coach service will be strengthened; The frequency of local franchised bus B routes connecting various land BCPs will also be enhanced beyond the normal weekend level; and The PTOs concerned will arrange additional vehicles and manpower to meet passenger demand. Travel during non-peak hours It is anticipated that the waiting time for PT services, including the Gold Bus and the franchised bus B routes, may be longer. Travellers should avoid travelling during peak hours as far as possible. Passengers are advised to maintain order while queuing and heed the advice of on-site Police and staff of PTOs concerned. Passengers planning to take cross-boundary coaches are also advised to reserve their coach tickets in advance. HZMB users travelling to Zhuhai should note that the temporary link bridge connecting the HZMB Zhuhai Port and Qinglu South Road has been closed to all traffic, and the traffic at Zhuhai Port and neighbouring roads has become very busy during holiday peak periods. They should use PT services as far as possible, plan their trips early, allow sufficient travelling time and remain patient while waiting. Motorists of cross-boundary private cars are advised that special traffic arrangements may be implemented at Shenzhen Bay Port, subject to actual traffic conditions, before and after the Chung Yeung Festival holiday to secure smooth access for PT vehicles to the Port. Cross-boundary private cars may experience longer waiting times for crossing the Port during peak periods. Motorists should pay extra attention to variable message signs and traffic signs along the roads. In case of traffic congestion, they should remain patient and follow the instructions of on-site Police. Information dissemination To plan their journeys ahead, members of the public can make use of the TD's HKeMobility mobile app or website ( hkemobility.gov.hk/en/traffic-information/live/cctv ) to access snapshots of traffic conditions of major connecting roads to land BCPs and the inbound and outbound vehicle plazas of the HZMB Hong Kong Port. They can also check the real-time situation at the vehicle clearance plaza of Zhuhai Port through the WeChat official accounts "hzmbzhport" or "zhuhaifabu" ( traffic-info.gzazhka.com:5015/#/ ) (Chinese only). Moreover, motorists are reminded to always comply with traffic control measures implemented by the Zhuhai authority when driving on the HZMB Main Bridge. Vehicles must not occupy the emergency lane unless instructed by the Zhuhai authority. The public and visitors may visit the one-stop information platform on immigration clearance "Easy Boundary" ( www.sb.gov.hk/eng/bwt/status.html?type=outbound ) of the Security Bureau or HKeMobility for the latest information on various land BCPs more conveniently. The TD will provide information on the services and waiting times of the Gold Bus and MTR. Members of the public are advised to check the latest traffic news through radio and television broadcasts, the TD's website ( www.td.gov.hk ) and HKeMobility. PTOs and relevant departments of BCPs will also disseminate the latest information to passengers through public announcement systems and other channels at major stations and BCPs. The TD's Emergency Transport Co-ordination Centre operates round the clock to closely monitor the traffic conditions and PT services across various districts, BCPs and major stations, and to implement contingency measures when necessary to meet service demand.

items.title: Grading of beach water quality released
items.description: The Environmental Protection Department (EPD) today (October 16) released the latest grading of water quality for 39 gazetted beaches (see Note 1) and one non-gazetted beach (see Note 2). Twenty-four beaches were rated as Good (Grade 1) and 16 as Fair (Grade 2). Grade 1 beaches are: Cafeteria New Beach* Lo So Shing Beach Cafeteria Old Beach Lower Cheung Sha Beach Cheung Chau Tung Wan Beach* Pui O Beach* Chung Hom Kok Beach Repulse Bay Beach* Clear Water Bay First Beach* Shek O Beach* Clear Water Bay Second Beach* South Bay Beach* Discovery Bay Tai Pak Beach St. Stephen's Beach* Hap Mun Bay Beach* Stanley Main Beach* Hung Shing Yeh Beach* Tai Po Lung Mei Beach* Kadoorie Beach* Tong Fuk Beach Kiu Tsui Beach Trio Beach* Kwun Yam Beach Upper Cheung Sha Beach Grade 2 beaches are: Anglers' Beach* Hoi Mei Wan Beach* Approach Beach* Lido Beach* Big Wave Bay Beach* Ma Wan Tung Wan Beach* Butterfly Beach* Middle Bay Beach* Casam Beach* Silver Mine Bay Beach* Castle Peak Beach Silverstrand Beach* Deep Water Bay Beach* Ting Kau Beach* Golden Beach* Turtle Cove Beach Compared with the grading released last week, Cafeteria Old Beach and Clear Water Bay Second Beach have been upgraded from Grade 2 to Grade 1. Middle Bay Beach has been changed from Grade 1 to Grade 2. "The changes in beach water quality are generally within the normal range of natural fluctuation," an EPD spokesman said. Under the present grading system, beaches are classified into four grades, namely Good (Grade 1), Fair (Grade 2), Poor (Grade 3) and Very Poor (Grade 4), according to the level of E. coli in the water. Grades are calculated on the basis of the geometric mean of the E. coli counts on the five most recent sampling occasions. While the ratings represent the general water quality at the beaches, the EPD spokesman reminded members of the public that water quality could be temporarily affected during and after periods of heavy rain. Bathers should avoid swimming at beaches for up to three days after a tropical cyclone or heavy rainfall. A summary of beach grades is published weekly before the weekend. The latest beach grades based on the most current data may be obtained from the EPD's website on Beach Water Quality ( www.epd.gov.hk/epd/beach ) or the beach hotline, 2511 6666. Members of the public can also obtain the latest daily water quality forecast information for all beaches that are open for swimming through the EPD's dedicated webpage on the beach water quality forecast ( www.epd.gov.hk/en/BWQForecast ). Note 1: Lifesaving services are provided by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department at 29 gazetted beaches, marked with an asterisk (*) above, from September 1. For details, please refer to the Leisure and Cultural Services Department's Special Announcement ( www.lcsd.gov.hk/en/beach/index.html ). Note 2: This refers to Discovery Bay Tai Pak Beach which has no lifesaving service.

items.title: Special traffic and transport arrangements for peak periods of passenger flow at Huanggang Port (with video)
items.description: The Transport Department (TD) said today (October 16) that special traffic and public transport arrangements will be implemented at the Huanggang Port during peak periods of passenger flow during the three-day holiday before and after the Chung Yeung Festival starting tomorrow (October 17) and in future to expedite passenger dispersal and provide convenience for the public and visitors. The public should plan their journeys early, choose suitable control points for boundary crossing based on their needs, and need not rush to use the new port. A spokesman for the TD said, "We have formulated various traffic contingency plans jointly with relevant departments and public transport operators (PTOs). These include comprehensively increasing public transport service frequencies, enhancing passenger dispersal efficiency at major interchanges, flexibly adjusting traffic signals and implementing alternative routes, taking a multipronged approach to ensure smooth overall traffic at the Huanggang Port. Cross-boundary travellers should make use of the new feature in the HKeMobility mobile app to check interchange information of the Huanggang Port and the San Tin Public Transport Interchange (PTI) for smart travel." Public transport arrangements The TD has steered franchised bus, green minibus (GMB) and cross-boundary coach (CBC) operators to deploy additional standby vehicles and manpower to strengthen services to meet passenger demand. During peak hours, franchised bus service frequencies can be increased to every two to three minutes, while GMB and CBC frequencies can be raised to every three to four minutes. Apart from the 24-hour close monitoring of traffic and transport conditions of the Huanggang Port by the TD's Emergency Transport Co-ordination Centre, the TD and PTOs will also deploy additional staff for on-site monitoring at the Huanggang Port PTI, major interchanges, major bus termini and stops with higher passenger demand along routes to and from the port. They will monitor changes in passenger and traffic flows in real time to flexibly deploy resources to cater for diverse travel needs of passengers. Of note, the TD has put up public transport overviews at the queueing areas and key locations of the San Tin PTI, enabling passengers to grasp information on franchised bus and GMB routes connecting the port and various districts at a glance. Currently, passengers at the San Tin PTI can interchange for bus services directly to seven MTR stations across three MTR lines; interchange for three bus routes to North District; or take Long Win Bus route No. A43P to the airport and the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge Hong Kong Port. Queueing order on site will also be enhanced to improve dispersal efficiency. In addition, the TD has rearranged the spatial layout of the San Tin PTI, arranging for tour coaches to pick up and drop off passengers at the locations closest to the air-conditioned waiting area, enhancing the travel experience. Information has been issued by the TD through the Travel Industry Authority and the Travel Industry Council of Hong Kong to travel agencies and visitors to assist them in planning their journeys in advance and selecting suitable bus services to travel between the Huanggang Port and the San Tin PTI. Information dissemination A button for the Huanggang Port has been added to the TD's HKeMobility app, allowing users to conveniently check the public transport interchange overview at their fingertips, plan their journeys early and select suitable routes to and from the port. Various PTOs will also step up dissemination of information on increased frequencies of routes concerned, interchange routes or concessions for passenger convenience.

items.title: Hong Kong Science Museum's "2026 The Future Science Prize Exhibition" showcases achievements of laureates (with photos)
items.description: The Hong Kong Science Museum (HKScM) is presenting the "2026 The Future Science Prize Exhibition" from today (October 16) to November 18 at the Exhibition Hall on the ground floor. The exhibition this year will focus on science in daily life, showcasing the outstanding contributions of this year's three laureates and Hong Kong laureates over the years to allow visitors to learn more about their scientific achievements. Established in 2016, the Future Science Prize presents three awards every year aiming to give recognition to scientists who have achieved outstanding scientific results on the Chinese Mainland, in Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan, with the goal of inspiring China, the world and the next generation with the spirit of science. The Life Science Prize laureate of the Future Science Prize this year is Dr Zhang Hong for pioneering contributions to the mechanism and physiological function of autophagy specific in multicellular organisms. The Physical Science Prize is awarded to Professor Zhao Dongyuan for pioneering contributions to mesoporous materials in the context of synthetic control, mechanistic understanding and industrial application. Professor Yuan Xinyi receives the Mathematics and Computer Science Prize for his fundamental contributions to arithmetic geometry. A number of multimedia and interactive exhibits are on display, which allow visitors to explore the relevant scientific knowledge and applications of award-winning fields in the past, including cryptography, catalysis and hepatitis virus, in a simple way. The "Digital Fingerprint Lab" invites visitors to experience the magic of cryptography in detecting forgery and to explore the research of Professor Wang Xiaoyun, laureate of the 2019 Mathematics and Computer Science Prize; the interactive exhibit "Mechanism of Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Infection of Liver Cells" showcases the groundbreaking research of Professor Li Wenhui, laureate of the 2022 Life Science Prize, who discovered how a specific receptor on the surface of human liver cells is exploited by hepatitis B and D viruses to cause infection; and the "Catalysis Reaction Simulator" allows visitors to learn about the research of Professor Zhang Tao and Professor Li Yadong, laureates of the 2024 Physical Science Prize, in the field of Single-Atom Catalysis and to explore how this technology enhances industrial efficiency. In addition, the 2026 Future Science Prize Week will take place during the exhibition period. One of its highlight events, Science Symposiums, will be held on November 6 and 7 at the Lecture Hall of the HKScM, where world-renowned scientists will share scientific discoveries on cutting-edge topics. For details of the exhibition and activities, please visit the website at hk.science.museum/en/web/scm/exhibition/fsp.html .

items.title: HKICL alerts public of fraudulent website
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority: Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Limited (HKICL) has recently noted a fraudulent website at fpsrefund.club purported to be from HKICL. The fraudulent website imitates as "Buyer Online Protection" to provide services including 1) refund to buyer, 2) unauthorised online transaction reporting, and 3) online transaction support, for online transaction over FPS payment. It intends to trick user into giving away personal document number and ID photo together with phone number for real name verification in order to get cash reward. In addition, it also tricks user into providing bank name, bank account number and bank account holder's name to top up and withdraw money from its platform's virtual wallet. Further, it directs user to a fraudster impersonating as customer service personnel. Please be reminded that the fraudulent website may have multiple combinations at the end of the link, e.g.: fpsrefund.club/page/place_an_order/?uuid=refund ​HKICL advises that this fraudulent website has no affiliation with HKICL, or any business of HKICL. HKICL will not directly provide FPS service to individual members of the public or contact individual members of the public proactively under usual circumstance. The genuine official website addresses of HKICL are www.hkicl.com.hk and fps.hkicl.com.hk . HKICL urges the public to beware of suspicious calls, websites or other communications, and to remain vigilant in protecting personal information. If members of the public receive any suspicious communication purportedly from HKICL, please call HKICL's general line at 2533 1111 to verify. Members of the public who suspect that they have become the victim of fraudulent acts should report promptly to the Police.

items.title: CHP continues to implement multipronged strategy to curb spread of Mpox
items.description: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) today (October 16) recorded an imported Mpox (also known as Monkeypox) case. There has been a significant increase in Mpox cases in Hong Kong since August 2026. To curb the spread of Mpox, the CHP has adopted a multipronged approach, including conducting comprehensive epidemiological investigation and analysis to break transmission chains, enhancing collaboration with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to facilitate vaccination for individuals with high-risk exposure and increase their willingness to receive the Mpox vaccine, and strengthening public awareness and education efforts. The multipronged strategy has yielded initial effects. The number of confirmed cases recorded in the first 15 days of October has dropped significantly by more than 60 per cent compared to the same period last month (September), while the number of vaccination doses administered under the Mpox vaccination programme in the first two weeks of October has increased by more than 60 per cent compared to the same period last month. The CHP will continue to put in place various targeted prevention and control measures to safeguard public health. Strengthening prevention ------------------------------ Mpox vaccine can prevent infection and severe disease. Since late September, the CHP has set up an additional Mpox vaccination centre at the CHP Building, in addition to regular vaccination venues established by the Government. The CHP has also collaborated with three NGOs (namely Community Health Organisation for Intervention, Care and Empowerment; Hong Kong AIDS Foundation; and Hong Kong Christian Service) to provide outreach vaccination services during holidays and outside regular office hours, providing convenience and incentives to encourage individuals with high-risk contacts to get vaccinated as soon as possible. Along with the existing vaccination venues, the CHP has successfully administered the Mpox vaccine to approximately 650 high-risk individuals over the past month. The DH's Yau Ma Tei Integrated Treatment Centre (YMTITC) will also arrange an additional vaccination session (10am to 1pm) next Saturday (October 24). People with high-risk contact may call the YMTITC at 2195 6588 from Monday through Friday from 8.30am to 5pm to schedule an appointment. The vaccination venue is located on 7/F, Yau Ma Tei Jockey Club Polyclinic, 145 Battery Street, Yau Ma Tei. Vaccination provides a highly effective protective barrier. Studies show that receiving two doses of the Mpox vaccine reduces the risk of infection by 82 per cent, which significantly lowers the risk of transmission to sexual partners, and protects both the vaccinated individual and others. Local data also show that vaccinated patients are 87 per cent less likely to experience viral spread to other parts of the body. The CHP will continue to actively expand the number of Mpox vaccination venues and time slots to further reduce the risk of infection and transmission in the community. At the same time, the CHP's Mpox hotline (2125 2373) continues to provide health assessments and advice to high-risk individuals. The hotline will arrange individuals in need to get vaccinated inside the CHP. The hotline operates daily from 9am to 6pm. Case details -------------- The newly reported imported case involves a 36-year-old man who developed a fever, sore throat and rash over various parts of his body (including genital area, trunk, hands and legs) on October 10. As his symptoms continued to worsen, he called the CHP's Mpox hotline on October 13 and was arranged to receive isolation treatment at Princess Margaret Hospital on the same day. His condition is now stable. Upon laboratory testing by the CHP's Public Health Laboratory Services Branch (PHLSB), his clinical specimen tested positive for the Monkeypox virus. According to the information provided by the patient, he had high-risk sexual exposure outside Hong Kong during the incubation period. The CHP is continuing its epidemiological investigation of the case, and will report it to the World Health Organization. Since 2022, Hong Kong has recorded 116 Mpox cases (91 local cases and 25 imported cases). All patients are males. Epidemiological investigations revealed that among the 23 cases recorded since August, all patients reported having engaged in high-risk sexual activities during the incubation period, including having sex with male strangers or multiple partners, and having sex without a condom. Most of them have not received the Mpox vaccinations. The CHP's PHLSB conducted genetic analysis of the virus and found that some cases had identical genetic sequences, suggesting the existence of multiple transmission chains among men who have sex with men (MSM) population. Among the cases recorded since August, patients commonly used specific dating apps to find casual male sexual partners. After testing positive, some patients were unable to contact their newly met sexual partners, which hindered the CHP's ability to conduct effective contact tracing and implement corresponding prevention and control measures. In view of this, the CHP has increased its outreach on social media platforms to promote Mpox prevention and vaccination, and has collaborated with the operators of relevant dating apps to regularly push information about Mpox prevention and vaccination to all users in Hong Kong. The CHP urges individuals who have engaged in high-risk sexual contact, particularly with male strangers, to remain vigilant and take appropriate personal protective measures, including receiving the Mpox vaccination and avoiding high-risk sexual contact, so as to lower the risk of infection. Members of the public should retain their sexual partners' contact information to facilitate contact tracing when necessary. The CHP consistently conducts comprehensive and in-depth epidemiological investigations into every Mpox case, striving to contact individuals who have had high-risk contact with the patients to break the transmission chains within specific population. If the CHP identifies a specific venue as posing a transmission risk, it advises the premises to close temporarily to safeguard public health. CHP staff have also visited various entertainment venues frequented by MSM, including saunas, to promote Mpox prevention. Recently, "Hutong" on Shanghai Street, Mong Kok, has temporarily closed as per the CHP's advice. The CHP appeals once again to the public who visited "Hutong" on or after September 14, especially those who have had sexual contact with male strangers on the premises, to call the Mpox hotline as soon as possible. The CHP will then provide health assessments and advice. The CHP will also arrange persons with relevant symptoms to undergo testing. More information on Mpox --------------------------------- Mpox is not transmitted through respiratory droplets or aerosols in general, and transmission would not occur through social contact. The CHP reminds the public, especially those at higher risk of exposure, to take precautions and avoid close physical contact with persons or animals suspected of being infected. They should seek medical attention as soon as possible if they experience relevant symptoms, including rash, fever, chills, swollen lymph nodes, exhaustion, muscle pain, and severe headaches. They should not engage in activities with others that may involve contact with skin rash or body fluids. The DH has been providing Mpox vaccination services for high-risk groups, including individuals with high-risk sexual practices (such as having multiple sexual partners), sex workers, or having a history of sexually transmitted infection within the past 12 months. For more details, please visit the CHP's webpages on Mpox and the Mpox Vaccination Programme .

items.title: Speech by SITI at Launch Ceremony of HKUST RAISe+ Project Fund (English only) (with photo)
items.description: Following is the speech by the Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry, Professor Sun Dong, at the Launch Ceremony of the HKUST RAISe+ (Research, Academic and Industry Sectors One-plus) Project Fund today (October 16): Chairperson Shih (Vice-Chairperson of the University Council of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST), Ms Edith Shih), Professor Cheng (Vice-President for Research and Development of the HKUST, Professor Tim Cheng), distinguished guests, faculty members and researchers, Good morning. It is my honour to be here today at the Launch Ceremony of the HKUST RASIe+ Project Fund. Universities play an important role in Hong Kong’s development as an international innovation and technology centre. They advance knowledge, nurture talent, and develop innovative technologies to address real-world challenges. Yet, promising research must be validated to meet market needs before it can be transformed into viable products and services. This requires close collaboration among the Government, industry, academia, and research and investment sectors. This is why we initiated the Research, Academic and Industry Sectors One-plus (RAISe+) Scheme in 2023. Since then, the $10 billion Scheme has paved the way to connect universities’ R&D (research and development) outcomes with industry capital and real market demand. To date, 73 projects have been approved under the Scheme, with Government funding commitment of over $3 billion. I am pleased to see the HKUST’s active participation in this Scheme, with 19 projects supported so far. They cover a range of technology areas, including medical applications, artificial intelligence and environmental solutions, demonstrating the potential for university research outcomes to address practical needs across different sectors. I am delighted that the HKUST has taken one step further to launch the RAISe+ Project Fund that complements the Government’s efforts. By providing additional institutional support for research teams, the Fund helps promising projects progress from research and development towards practical applications. This also aligns with the direction set out in Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan announced last month, which emphasises our basic scientific research capabilities in original innovation and the role of institutions in attracting and cultivating talent for technological innovation. As announced in the 2026 Policy Address, the Government is exploring the establishment of the Innovation and Technology Application Scenario Promotion Centre. By matching excellent innovative technologies with the practical needs of public and private organisations, the Centre aims to provide more opportunities for promising local research outcomes to be tested, validated and finally commercialised. At the same time, the Government will continue to support university knowledge transfer through our annual funding provided to the Technology Transfer Offices of local universities. Ladies and gentlemen, RAISe+ is meant to be a bridge between Hong Kong’s research excellence and real market needs. The launch of the HKUST’s RAISe+ Project Fund today is an example of how universities can complement the Government’s initiative and contribute to this common objective. I look forward to seeing more research teams work closely with industry partners to bring promising technologies into practical use, creating value for our economy and society. My congratulations go to the HKUST once again on the launch of the Fund, and I wish the initiative every success. Thank you very much.

items.title: Government announces rollout of new batch of signature tourism projects by Working Group on Developing Tourist Hotspots (with photos)
items.description: The Government announced today (October 16) that the Working Group on Developing Tourist Hotspots (Working Group), led by the Deputy Chief Secretary for Administration, Mr Cheuk Wing-hing, will progressively roll out four projects during the next phase starting from the fourth quarter of 2026, to provide visitors with more diversified tourism experiences with Hong Kong characteristics. Mr Cheuk said, "In response to the growing pursuit of in-depth tourism experiences by visitors to Hong Kong, the Government has been committed to identifying and integrating tourism resources with potential in Hong Kong. Through strengthening cross-departmental co-ordination and leveraging community efforts, the nine tourist hotspot projects rolled out in the first phase have been well received. Starting from the end of this year, the Working Group will roll out tourist hotspot projects covering themes such as industrial brands, miniature art, religious culture and local characteristics in phases, showcasing Hong Kong's unique cultural heritage and city landscape to visitors." Details of the four projects are as follows: 1. Phase two of the Hong Kong industrial brand tourism The Hong Kong industrial brand tourism scheme has been well received since its launch. The next phase will further introduce different types of brands to provide visitors with more diversified options. The newly added projects include the depots of Kowloon Motor Bus, the MTR "Station Rail Voyage: Explorer" exhibition, and the Beijing Tong Ren Tang's Hong Kong production and research and development base. Visitors can visit the relevant brand facilities through a "group-in, group-out" mode to learn about the history of the brands and the production processes of related products. The Travel Industry Council of Hong Kong will continue to be commissioned to handle the reservation and co-ordination work of local travel agents. The visit arrangements for the relevant projects are expected to be progressively rolled out from the fourth quarter of this year. 2. Hong Kong Miniature City Exhibition To enrich the tourism experience at the Peak, Madame Tussauds Hong Kong will recreate the "Hong Kong Miniature City Exhibition" at the Peak Tower starting from the fourth quarter of this year. The new exhibition will feature exquisite new miniature art exhibits that vividly showcase Hong Kong's landmark buildings, authentic customs and ways of life in three dimensions, allowing visitors to savour the unique charm of Hong Kong while touring the Peak. 3. Promoting immersive religious and cultural tours To enhance tourists' sightseeing experiences through the use of technology, the Chinese Temples Committee is progressively strengthening the digitalisation and cultural promotion measures for its administered temples, such as installing QR code display boards at the temples, and allowing visitors to learn about temple antiquities and redeem cultural souvenirs by mobile application in an interactive manner. The Government will further explore using temples as the core to connect historical buildings and monuments of cultural value across various districts, thereby creating itineraries for "immersive temple culture tours". 4. Seasons of Yuen Long district tourism promotion project ​To promote the distinctive cultural landscape of urban-rural integration in Yuen Long, the Yuen Long District Office will collaborate with district organisations to launch the Seasons of Yuen Long project, with a view to encouraging visitors to explore the local characteristics of the district under different themes all year round (for example, viewing the grand parade in Yuen Long town centre during the Tin Hau Festival, and visiting the district’s natural and ecological attractions during autumn and winter to see red leaves and observe migratory birds). The project comprises the production of a tourist map, the development of a thematic website, and the installation of themed information boards near landmarks in the town centre and rural areas of Yuen Long. Deliverables are expected to be rolled out in phases from the fourth quarter of this year to the first quarter of next year. The Working Group expresses its gratitude to the organisations and brands involved in the above projects for their active participation and support. The Government will continue to promote cross-sectoral collaboration and encourage the trade to continuously develop tourism projects that can showcase different characteristics of Hong Kong, enriching visitors' experiences in the city, encouraging them to extend their stays, and attracting them to visit Hong Kong again.

items.title: Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Tax Deductions for Intellectual Property Expenditure) Bill 2026 gazetted
items.description: The Government published the Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Tax Deductions for Intellectual Property Expenditure) Bill 2026 (the Bill) today (October 16) to suitably relax the tax deduction arrangements for relevant capital expenditure incurred by enterprises for purchasing Intellectual Property (IP) rights or for the licence to use IP rights. A spokesman for the Commerce and Economic Development Bureau said, "The Bill puts into effect the measure announced in the 2025-26 and 2026-27 Budgets to further enhance the tax deduction arrangements for local IP, lowering the costs of IP transactions to facilitate more IP trading activities and support the development of knowledge‑intensive industries in Hong Kong." The Bill proposes to relax the IP-related tax deduction arrangements by allowing tax deductions for relevant capital expenditure incurred by enterprises in respect of the following: (1) Purchase of eligible IP rights from associates: allowing tax deduction for capital expenditure incurred by enterprises for the purchase of eligible IP rights from associates, such as group affiliates, to encourage multinational enterprises to centralise their IP management in Hong Kong, and to facilitate domestic intra-group transfer and business activities; (2) Purchase of eligible IP rights which are used by a licensee outside Hong Kong: where the licensing income from the eligible IP rights is regarded as arising in or derived from Hong Kong under the foreign-sourced income exemption regime and is chargeable to profits tax in Hong Kong, the capital expenditure incurred for the purchase of the IP rights may also be allowed for tax deduction on a proportionate basis; and (3) Upfront licence fee for the use of eligible IP rights in a licensing arrangement: to further encourage IP development and commercialisation, tax deduction can be allowed for upfront licence fees incurred by enterprises for the use of eligible IP rights in a licensing arrangement. ​ The amendments proposed in the Bill will apply to contracts entered into on or after April 1, 2026, for the purchase of eligible IP rights or for the licence to use eligible IP rights. To safeguard Hong Kong's tax base and prevent abuse of the tax deduction arrangements, the Bill provides for a series of rigorous safeguard measures. These include introducing a main purpose test for the purchase of IP rights from associates, providing for the calculation of the deduction amount for the capital expenditure incurred for the purchase of IP rights from Hong Kong associates, and where the capital expenditure incurred for purchasing eligible IP rights from non-Hong Kong business associates or acquiring a licence from associates for the use of eligible IP rights exceeds a specified threshold, a third-party independent valuation report is required to substantiate the tax deduction claim, so as to prevent excessive tax deduction. The spokesman continued, "The Government has been actively promoting the development of IP trading and financing in Hong Kong. Following the implementation of the concessionary tax rate under the 'patent box' initiative, the Bill will further enhance Hong Kong's IP tax ecosystem. The introduction of more flexible tax deduction arrangements, whilst upholding our tax principles, will incentivise more local and overseas enterprises to select Hong Kong as their preferred platform for cross-border technology transfer and IP financing, thereby bolstering Hong Kong's development into an international innovation and technology centre and a regional IP trading centre, in alignment with the National 15th Five-Year Plan." The Bill will be introduced into the Legislative Council for First Reading and Second Reading on October 28.

items.title: Subsidiary legislation relating to implementation of new arrangement on mutual service of judicial documents in civil and commercial proceedings gazetted
items.description: The Government today (October 16) published in the Gazette the subsidiary legislation relating to the implementation of the Arrangement on Mutual Service of Judicial Documents in Civil and Commercial Proceedings between the Mainland and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (New Arrangement), namely, the Rules of the High Court (Amendment) (No. 2) Rules 2026, Rules of the District Court (Amendment) (No. 2) Rules 2026 and Matrimonial Causes (Amendment) Rules 2026. The aforesaid subsidiary legislation will come into operation on March 30, 2027. The existing Arrangement for Mutual Service of Judicial Documents in Civil and Commercial Proceedings between the Mainland and Hong Kong Courts (Existing Arrangement) has been implemented for over 27 years. The volume of requests for mutual service of judicial documents between the courts of the two places has surged in recent years. To enhance the efficiency of the courts of the two places in mutual service of judicial documents, the Department of Justice (DoJ) and the Supreme People's Court (SPC) signed the New Arrangement on April 20 this year with a view to enhancing the mechanism for mutual service of judicial documents in civil and commercial matters between the Mainland and Hong Kong. The New Arrangement aims to further promote the alignment of mechanisms and rules between the legal systems of the two places. The above subsidiary legislation seeks to implement the New Arrangement in Hong Kong, while the SPC will promulgate judicial interpretation on the implementation of the New Arrangement in the Mainland. The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and SPC have agreed that the New Arrangement will come into force on March 30, 2027, replacing the Existing Arrangement. In order to implement the New Arrangement, the High Court Rules Committee made the Rules of the High Court (Amendment) (No. 2) Rules 2026 under section 54 of the High Court Ordinance (Cap. 4) on October 12, 2026; the District Court Rules Committee made the Rules of the District Court (Amendment) (No. 2) Rules 2026 under section 72 of the District Court Ordinance (Cap. 336) on October 12, 2026; and the Chief Judge made the Matrimonial Causes (Amendment) Rules 2026 under section 54 of the Matrimonial Causes Ordinance (Cap. 179) on October 12, 2026. A spokesman for the DoJ said, "The relevant subsidiary legislation implements the New Arrangement to add manners of service of judicial documents for civil proceedings (including matrimonial proceedings) on persons in the Mainland, thereby promoting timely and efficient handling of cross-boundary civil and commercial cases, strengthening the protection of the rights and interest of parties in the two places and better accommodating the increasingly close-knit ties and judicial needs between the Mainland and Hong Kong." The Government briefed the Legislative Council Panel on Administration of Justice and Legal Services on the signing and implementation work of the New Arrangement on April 27, 2026. The Panel and the representatives of the Law Society of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Bar Association generally welcomed the signing and supported the implementation of the New Arrangement. The Government also consulted the relevant stakeholders including the two legal professional bodies on the draft amendment rules of the courts and has suitably incorporated their comments. The above subsidiary legislation will be tabled at the Legislative Council next Wednesday (October 21) for negative vetting.

items.title: Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes (General) (Amendment) Regulation 2025 (Commencement) Notice gazetted
items.description: The Government published in the Gazette today (October 16) the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes (General) (Amendment) Regulation 2025 (Commencement) Notice (Commencement Notice) to appoint December 21 as the day on which the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes (General) (Amendment) Regulation 2025 (L.N. 206 of 2025) (the Amendment Regulation) comes into operation. The Amendment Regulation was enacted by the Legislative Council (LegCo) on September 26, 2025, to provide the legal basis for implementing Phase One of Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) "Full Portability", with the exact implementation date to be announced through a notice published in the Gazette. Under the Amendment Regulation, employees whose employment commences on or after May 1, 2025 (New EEs), may transfer accrued benefits derived from employer mandatory contributions in respect of the current employment in its entire amount from a contribution account of the MPF scheme participated in by the employer to a personal account of an MPF scheme of their own choice, once in every calendar year or more than once in every calendar year if the governing rules of the MPF scheme from which the accrued benefits are transferred so provide. The Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, Mr Christopher Hui, said, "With the upcoming implementation of Phase One 'Full Portability' on December 21, we have fulfilled our commitment set out in the 2026 Policy Address to implement Phase One 'Full Portability' within 2026. This will strengthen New EEs' control over their MPF benefits, encourage them to more proactively manage their MPF investments, promote market competition, and create room for fee reductions. In relation to Phase Two 'Full Portability' which will benefit the remaining employees, we are preparing the relevant legislative proposal and will introduce an amendment bill into the LegCo by mid-2027." The Commencement Notice will be tabled before the LegCo next Wednesday (October 21) for the negative vetting procedure.

items.title: Official ceremony to commemorate 160th anniversary of birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen
items.description: The Government announced today (October 16) that an official ceremony will be held on November 12 to commemorate the 160th anniversary of the birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen. November 12, 2026, marks the 160th anniversary of the birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen, a great national hero, a great patriot and a great forerunner of China's democratic revolution. In commemoration of Dr Sun Yat-sen's immortal contributions to national independence, social progress and the people's well-being, the Government will hold an official ceremony at Sun Yat Sen Memorial Park on the morning of November 12. Hongkong Post will issue special stamps to commemorate the 160th anniversary of the birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen on the same day. Government departments and community organisations will organise a series of commemorative activities starting this month to allow members of the public to gain a better understanding of his life and contributions from diverse perspectives. These activities include exhibitions, seminars, guided tours, film screenings, student and youth exchange tours to the Chinese Mainland, local heritage trail visits, and a parent-child quiz competition. Information on relevant activities has been uploaded to the thematic webpage "Commemoration of the 160th anniversary of the birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen", which was added to the official website of the Dr Sun Yat-sen Museum today. Members of the public are welcome to browse the thematic webpage for the commemoration of the 160th anniversary of the birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen for details of the activities.

items.title: Labour Department to hold online briefing for employers of foreign domestic helpers
items.description: The Labour Department (LD) will hold an online briefing on the employment of foreign domestic helpers (FDHs) on November 19 (Thursday), at 7pm. Enrolment is now open. The online briefing will provide an overview of the employment rights and obligations of employers of FDHs. Representatives from the Immigration Department will also speak on the Immigration Ordinance and legislation related to the employment of FDHs, as well as to share insights on building a safe community. Employers of FDHs, especially first-time employers, are welcome to attend. The online briefing will be conducted in Cantonese via Zoom, and admission is free. Interested parties may register online at the LD's dedicated FDH Portal ( www.fdh.labour.gov.hk ), or download the enrolment form ( www.fdh.labour.gov.hk/res/pdf/Enrolment_Form_ER.pdf ) and submit it by email ( fdh-enquiry@labour.gov.hk ) or by fax (3101 0604). The deadline for enrolment is November 17 (Tuesday). The quota will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. For enquiries, please contact the LD at 3582 8995.

items.title: Applications invited for Research Fellowship Scheme under Health and Medical Research Fund
items.description: The Health Bureau today (October 16) invited interested parties to apply for the Research Fellowship Scheme under the Health and Medical Research Fund (HMRF). The scheme aims to support researchers or professionals, particularly healthcare professionals, in their early to mid-career to enhance their skills in public health and health services research. The grant ceiling per award is $1.2 million, inclusive of $400,000 for training outside Hong Kong. Tertiary institutions funded by the University Grants Committee (UGC) and Prince of Wales Hospital (PWH) and Queen Mary Hospital (QMH) are invited to nominate applicants for the scheme. Details of the number of nominations and number of awards are summarised in the table below: Streams Maximum number of nominations by each tertiary institution/ teaching hospital Total number of awards for each stream (Note) Stream A: UGC-funded tertiary institutions * The Chinese University of Hong Kong and the University of Hong Kong * Others 10 8 16 Stream B: PWH and QMH 8 4 Each applicant can only submit one application and may receive the research fellowship award only once. All previous awardees are ineligible to reapply. To tie in with the "Towards 2025: Strategy and Action Plan to Prevent and Control Non-communicable Diseases (NCDs) in Hong Kong" and the "Hong Kong Cancer Strategy 2019" launched by the Government, higher priority will be accorded to applications that address cancer and the preventable or modifiable risk factors for NCDs, namely unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, tobacco use and harmful use of alcohol. The application should cover: A training programme outside Hong Kong (regular programmes for higher academic qualifications, e.g. Master or PhD degrees will not be considered) with attachment to a reputable institution for at least three months cumulatively throughout the fellowship period; and A small-scale research project relating to the proposed training programme with no more than three research objectives. The HMRF emphasises the importance of the translational potential of research findings, and therefore supports applications on the following research projects: Clinical research including patient-oriented research, epidemiological and behavioural studies, outcomes research and health services research; Infectious diseases research with public health implications from bench to bedside and at community level and with translational value; and Clinical research based on Chinese medicine theory or clinical research on Chinese medicine theory and methodology. Applications will be subject to peer review. Shortlisted applicants will be invited for an interview. The assessment will take into account the capability of the applicant and his or her performance at the interview, the importance of the training proposal to healthcare development, as well as its relevance to the proposed research project. The proposed research project will be evaluated on its scientific merit, local context, and translational potential or value to public health or health services. Completed electronic application forms should be submitted via the electronic Grant Management System ( rfs.healthbureau.gov.hk/eGMS/ ) on or before 6pm on January 7, 2027 (Hong Kong time). The briefing session, which will be held on November 17, 2026, is now open for registration . For details, please refer to the website of the Research Fund Secretariat . For enquiries, please send an email to rfs@healthbureau.gov.hk . Note: The total number of awards granted will be subject to the quality and budget requirements of the applications.
