items.description: The 2026 final register for the Rural Representative Election (RRE) was published today (October 16). The final register contains the particulars of the registered electors of Existing Villages, Indigenous Villages, Composite Indigenous Villages and Market Towns. Registered electors may log into the RRE Voter Registration Information Enquiry System through the RRE website ( www.had.gov.hk/rre ) for perusal of their own registration particulars. They may also call the RRE hotline at 2152 1521 during ordinary business hours for enquiries about the relevant information. A full copy of the final register is placed at the office of the Electoral Registration Officer located at the Home Affairs Department (HAD), 11/F, Southorn Centre, 130 Hennessy Road, Wan Chai. Copies of the specific divisions of the final register for Rural Areas that belong to the Rural Committees concerned are placed at the offices of the Assistant Electoral Registration Officers in the respective New Territories District Offices (NTDOs), the office addresses of which are set out on the RRE website. Pursuant to section 30 of the Electoral Affairs Commission (Registration of Electors) (Rural Representative Election) Regulation (Cap. 541K), specified persons including members of the press (meaning persons who subscribe to the Government News and Media Information System maintained by the Director of Information Services), political parties (i.e. political bodies/organisations that meet the specified requirements under the Regulation), Heung Yee Kuk, respective Rural Committees for the relevant Rural Areas, indigenous inhabitants of the relevant Indigenous Villages or Composite Indigenous Villages, as well as residents of the relevant Existing Villages or Market Towns can inspect the aforementioned final register of electors for purposes relating to the RRE, by making an appointment through the RRE hotline or the relevant NTDOs during ordinary business hours starting from today. The ordinary business hours of the HAD and NTDOs in respect of the above matter are from 9am to 1pm and from 2pm to 6pm, Monday to Friday (except general holidays). Statistical information about the final register is available on the RRE website. For enquiries, please visit the RRE website or call the RRE hotline.

items.title: Government gazettes to include more endangered species on control list
items.description: The Government gazetted today (October 16) the Protection of Endangered Species of Animals and Plants Ordinance (Amendment of Schedules 1 and 3) Order 2026 (the Amendment Order) to amend Schedules 1 and 3 to the Protection of Endangered Species of Animals and Plants Ordinance (Cap. 586) (the Ordinance) so as to implement the latest list of endangered species subject to control under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). The 20th meeting of the Conference of the Parties was held in November and December 2025, at which Appendices I and II to CITES were amended, updating the list of endangered species subject to control. A spokesman for the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) said that CITES is implemented in Hong Kong through the Ordinance and hence the Ordinance is updated from time to time in light of the latest requirements of CITES. The Amendment Order aims to give effect to the latest regulations of CITES on the controlled species. The Amendment Order mainly reflects the addition, removal and other changes of species listed in the Appendices to CITES, and involves a number of species of sharks, manta rays and devil rays, wood and ornamental plants, etc. Major amendments are set out in the Annex. Under the Ordinance, except with exemptions or otherwise specified, the import, export, re-export, introduction from the sea, possession or control of specimens of scheduled species, including their parts and derivatives, are subject to licensing control. The Amendment Order will be tabled at the Legislative Council on October 21, 2026, for negative vetting, and the new control measures will come into effect on December 31, 2026, with the effective date for some species deferred to June 5, 2027, pursuant to the decisions adopted at the 20th meeting of the Conference of the Parties. A Licence to Possess must be obtained within the three-month grace period (i.e. on or before March 30, 2027) for the possession of specimens of Appendix I species or live specimens of wild origin of Appendix II species for commercial purposes. Local trading of the listed species which were already imported legally before the implementation of the new amendments can continue under licensing control. The AFCD will introduce to relevant traders and stakeholders the details of the amendments to the Ordinance through circular letters and briefing sessions. The spokesman said, "More endangered species will be included on the control list after the amendments to the Ordinance come into effect. This will help enhance protection of more endangered species and enable Hong Kong to make a contribution to nature conservation at an international level." The spokesman reminded the public that it is illegal for any person to import, export or possess any endangered species without a required licence. Offenders are liable to a maximum penalty of a $10 million fine and imprisonment for 10 years upon conviction. The specimens will also be forfeited. For licensing requirements for the species listed on different appendices, please visit the website: www.cites.hk . For enquiries, please contact the AFCD through email ( hk_cites@afcd.gov.hk ) or call 1823.

items.title: International Organizations (Privileges and Immunities) (The International Criminal Police Organization-INTERPOL) (231st Executive Committee Session and 94th General Assembly Session) Order gazetted
items.description: ​The International Organizations (Privileges and Immunities) (The International Criminal Police Organization-INTERPOL) (231st Executive Committee Session and 94th General Assembly Session) Order was gazetted today (October 16). The Central People's Government and The International Criminal Police Organization-INTERPOL (INTERPOL) signed an agreement on the granting of privileges and immunities to INTERPOL and the persons connected with it for the purposes of the 231st Executive Committee Session and 94th General Assembly (GA) session to be held in Hong Kong. The Order was made by the Chief Executive in Council under the International Organizations (Privileges and Immunities) Ordinance (Cap. 558). The Order seeks to implement the privileges and immunities as provided under the agreement. The GA is the highest governing body of INTERPOL. It meets yearly for representatives of member countries to discuss international policing issues and foster collaboration. The 94th GA will be held in Hong Kong from November 30 to December 3, 2026. The Executive Committee, chaired by the President of INTERPOL, is the governing body in charge of supervising the execution of the GA's decisions and the administration and work of the General Secretariat of INTERPOL. The 231st Executive Committee Session will be held in Hong Kong on November 29, 2026. A Government spokesperson said, "The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government will spare no effort in ensuring the successful delivery of the INTERPOL 231st Executive Committee Session and 94th GA, which will be hosted by our country in Hong Kong, to showcase to the world the achievements of the "one country, two systems" framework, and tell the good stories of our country, Hong Kong and the Police." The Order will be tabled before the Legislative Council on October 21, 2026, for negative vetting. The Order will come into operation on the same day.

items.title: Housing Authority highly concerned about serious deficiencies in lift replacement works at two estates under Tenants Purchase Scheme
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Housing Authority: The Hong Kong Housing Authority (HA) said on October 15 that it has been informed by the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department (EMSD) that there were serious deficiencies during the lift replacement works at two estates under the Tenants Purchase Scheme (TPS), namely Pok Hong Estate in Sha Tin and Tsui Ping (North) Estate in Kwun Tong, in 2025 and 2026 respectively. Although a fire resisting rating certificate was submitted regarding the fire resisting doorsets, including door frame components, it was found that only the fire resisting doors were installed as required, but Taizoom Elevator Company (HK) Limited did not install the corresponding door frame components. Though the absence of these door frame components in the lifts concerned is a non-compliance, the lifts can still operate safely. As the owner of the unsold units in the two aforementioned TPS estates, the HA is highly concerned about the incident. The HA is maintaining close contact with the EMSD to seriously follow up on the incident and pursue the liabilities of Taizoom Elevator Company (HK) Limited. Among all TPS estates, only the lift replacement works in the two aforementioned estates were undertaken by this company. For another TPS estate, Fu Heng Estate, which is currently preparing for lift replacement, the contract has not yet been awarded. The HA has immediately and proactively advised the Incorporated Owners of Fu Heng Estate to suspend the award of the contract, and will provide all necessary support to the Incorporated Owners regarding the incident, including assisting them in studying the follow-up arrangements, to safeguard the overall interests and safety of all residents.

items.title: EMSD's inspections reveal serious deficiencies in lift replacement works undertaken by registered lift contractor at two estates
items.description: ​In response to the recent allegations of non-compliance by Taizoom Elevator Company (HK) Limited (Taizoom), the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department (EMSD) takes the matter seriously and conducted surprise inspections on the lift works concerned. The inspections revealed serious deficiencies in lift replacement works carried out by Taizoom in two Tenants Purchase Scheme Estates, involving 9 lifts in Tsui Ping (North) Estate in Kwun Tong, of which the replacement was completed between February and July 2026, and 39 lifts in Pok Hong Estate in Sha Tin, of which the replacement was completed between May 2025 and July 2026. Regarding the fire resisting doorsets, including door frame components, although a fire resisting rating certificate was submitted, it was found that only the fire resisting doors were installed as required, but the corresponding door frame components were not installed, and the lift works were claimed to be completed. The absence of these door frame components in the lifts concerned is a non-compliance, but the lifts can still operate safely. The EMSD has instructed Taizoom to review the lifts at the aforementioned estates and install the outstanding door frame components promptly, and bear all associated costs for the remedial measures. The repair works will commence shortly and are expected to be completed within a month. The EMSD will proactively contact the property management companies of the concerned estates to provide necessary assistance. The lifts will need to be suspended from operation during the installation of new door frames. The works will be scheduled during non-peak hours as far as possible, and it is anticipated that the installation for each lift will take around one to two days to complete. During the installation period, the EMSD will closely monitor the installation works and maintain close contact with the relevant property management companies. The EMSD will also urge Taizoom to ensure that all lift lobbies and building passages are free from obstruction during the installation works, implement appropriate fire safety measures, and minimise the impact on residents. As preliminary evidence indicates that Taizoom is suspected of serious negligence or misconduct in carrying out lift works, the EMSD will take enforcement and regulatory actions in accordance with the Lifts and Escalators Ordinance. Under the circumstances, the EMSD cannot rule out the possibility that criminal offences involving fraud and the provision of false statements may have been committed, and will refer the case to the Hong Kong Police Force for further investigation. The EMSD will complete the inspection of all lifts installed by Taizoom throughout the territory within three days. The inspection includes re-examining the fire resisting rating certificates of fire resisting doorsets including their frame components, as well as checking if any door frame components are missing. The EMSD has also commenced inspections of lift engineering works undertaken by other registered lift contractors, and no similar breaches have been found so far. As a precautionary measure, the EMSD will require other registered lift contractors to conduct similar inspections on the lifts they have installed and submit inspection reports to the EMSD. The EMSD will also conduct random checks, and all related work is expected to be completed within a month. The EMSD has commenced a comprehensive review, encompassing the installation of new equipment and lift modernisation, inspection and maintenance works, evaluation of site supervision system, as well as the registration, regulation, and approval systems under the Lifts and Escalators Ordinance. Furthermore, the EMSD will enhance its inspections and spot checks on all lifts to improve overall works quality, with the review expected to be completed within the year. If any issues with lift engineering quality or deficiencies in the site supervision and inspection system are identified, immediate follow-up and improvement actions will be taken, along with strengthened inspections and audits of lifts.

items.title: HA appeals to public for a patient requiring urgent liver transplant
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Hospital Authority: The spokesperson for the Hospital Authority (HA) today (October 15) made the following appeal regarding a patient whose condition requires urgent liver transplant: A 13-year-old boy who requires an urgent liver transplant is currently hospitalised at Queen Mary Hospital and is in serious condition. The patient has been experiencing severe hepatic failure and developed severe complications including recurrent hyperammonemia and cholangitis. The patient is clinically assessed as requiring an urgent liver transplant and is listed at the top of the liver transplant waiting list for O+ blood group. In response to the urgent appeal from the patient's family, the HA appeals to members of the public to proactively support organ donation and consider donating the organ of a deceased relative to rekindle the lives of others. In view of the critical condition of the patient, in addition to proactively searching for a suitable liver locally, the HA will also seek assistance from the Mainland through the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government as soon as possible. When a patient who is willing to donate an organ passes away and no suitable patient is identified to receive the organ on the Mainland, the cross-boundary organ donation and matching mechanism will facilitate a transplant in Hong Kong to bring hope to a critically ill patient. The spokesperson emphasised that when a suitable liver is found, the HA will strictly follow the relevant organ transplant regulations and make an application with the authorities to ensure that all procedures comply with relevant standards and regulatory requirements. The HA will arrange transplant operations that aim to save the patient's life as soon as possible. For critically ill patients with organ failure, an organ transplant is often the only hope to extend their lives. When the families of deceased patients show a selfless act of love and donate the deceased person's organs to save dying patients, it not only gives critically ill patients the hope of life, but also eases the hardship of their families. The HA appeals to the public to pass on their great love, blessing and care to those who are still fighting for their well-deserved lives.

items.title: FS begins visit to Bangkok, Thailand (with photos/video)
items.description: ​The Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan, arrived in Bangkok, Thailand, today (October 15) to begin his visit, attending the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group and related events as a member of the Chinese delegation. Mr Chan attended a high-level roundtable co-organised by the IMF and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) to explore how economies in the Middle East and Central Asia can better benefit from the vast opportunities offered by Hong Kong's investment and financing markets. Heads of finance ministries and central banks from a number of countries in these regions took part. In his keynote speech, Mr Chan said that the increasingly close financial ties between Hong Kong and the Middle East and Central Asia help investors diversify their investments and enable enterprises to better raise capital for business development and manage risks. As these economies continue to develop and diversify, Hong Kong can support their growth in three areas: mobilising long-term capital, broadening currency options, and managing and sharing risks. On mobilising long-term capital, Mr Chan pointed out that Hong Kong's common law system under "one country, two systems", free flow of capital, Linked Exchange Rate System, diverse investor base, and connectivity with both Mainland and international capital markets provide a solid foundation for investment. Hong Kong ranked first globally in funds raised through initial public offerings last year. In the first nine months of this year, funds raised reached nearly US$50 billion, more than double the amount in the same period last year and already exceeding last year's full-year total. Hong Kong also supports industries in reducing emissions and transitioning to greener operations through green and sustainable finance. Infrastructure asset securitisation helps broaden the investor base and enables lenders to recycle capital into new projects. On broadening currency options, Mr Chan said that Hong Kong is continuing to enhance its offshore Renminbi (RMB) ecosystem to facilitate financing, settlement and investment by enterprises and investors. This helps enterprises with close business ties with the Mainland reduce currency conversion risks and better align the currencies of their receipts, payments and borrowings. Hong Kong has the world's largest offshore RMB liquidity pool, with deposits of around RMB1.3 trillion. With the support of the People's Bank of China, the HKMA expanded the funding arrangements supporting RMB trade business to RMB500 billion in July, further meeting enterprises' financing needs. On managing and sharing risks, Mr Chan noted that Hong Kong has facilitated seven issuances of catastrophe bonds totalling around US$800 million since 2021. These bonds bring in capital market investors to share catastrophe risks, providing additional protection against major disasters and strengthening the resilience of businesses and communities. Mr Chan invited international multilateral organisations, financial institutions and insurers to work together in innovative ways to promote more efficient capital mobilisation and risk management, enabling all parties to share in the benefits of economic development. He said that Hong Kong's concentration of relevant professional expertise, abundant capital and extensive experience can help structure projects to make them bankable, fostering a virtuous cycle in which investment drives growth and growth creates investment opportunities. The Chief Executive of the HKMA, Mr Eddie Yue, and senior management members of three major banks in Hong Kong also attended the roundtable. Mr Chan also called on the Chinese Ambassador to Thailand, Mr Zhang Jianwei, today to exchange views on Thailand's economy, China-Thailand relations and the international landscape. Mr Chan gave an update on Hong Kong's economy and an overview of the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030). The two sides also had in-depth exchanges on further strengthening economic and trade co-operation and people-to-people exchanges between Hong Kong and Thailand. He also met with the Regional Vice President for Asia and the Pacific of the International Finance Corporation, Mr Sarvesh Suri, for in-depth exchanges on strengthening co-operation in a number of areas. These included more effectively mobilising private capital to support sustainable development in infrastructure, education, healthcare and the digital economy in the region, and participating in the formulation of relevant international standards; strengthening financing support for trade, supply chains and small and medium-sized enterprises; using financial instruments such as catastrophe bonds to manage and share climate risks; and enhancing co-operation in talent training. Mr Chan will continue his visit to Bangkok tomorrow (October 16), including attending the plenary session of the Annual Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank Group.

items.title: Government announces quarterly land sale programme for October to December 2026
items.description: The Government announced today (October 15) the quarterly land sale programme for the third quarter of 2026-27, i.e. October to December 2026. The Secretary for Development, Ms Bernadette Linn, said the Government will put up for tender a site at the Junction of Tai Chung Kiu Road and On Sum Street, Shek Mun, Shatin, for private residential development in the third quarter of the 2026-27 financial year. The site has a floor space of around 48 090 square metres and can provide around 960 flats. The site is situated in a mature residential neighbourhood and in close proximity to Shek Mun MTR Station, with comprehensive surrounding infrastructure and traffic network. Originally zoned for commercial use, the site is selected from the Annual Land Sale List announced in February this year and has obtained planning approval from the Town Planning Board for private residential development. The prospective developer shall set aside some floor space for the provision of a public vehicle park on site which can be exempted from gross floor area calculations according to the policy announced last year. Apart from government land sale, other sources of private housing supply in this quarter include the Urban Renewal Authority's To Kwa Wan Road project, which is estimated to provide around 1 050 flats. As for private development and redevelopment projects, seven projects are expected to complete the lease modification or land exchange procedures in the third quarter, providing a total supply of around 1 835 flats, demonstrating developers' optimistic attitude towards market prospects. In addition, the Development Bureau had invited the market to submit expressions of interest for student hostel development at three commercial sites in Kai Tak, Siu Lek Yuen (Shatin) and Tung Chung East in January 2026, and received a positive response. The Development Bureau plans to put up for tender the Siu Lek Yuen (Shatin) site in this quarter, which is estimated to provide around 600 beds. The site is situated in close proximity to City One MTR Station and Shek Mun MTR Station, as well as nearby post-secondary institutions. Having regard to the tender result of the Siu Lek Yuen (Shatin) site, the Government will consider the way forward on the other two sites. "Taking all of the above sources of land supply into account, the total private housing land supply in the third quarter of this financial year would support the development of around 3 845 units. Together with the supply from the first two quarters of this financial year, the total private housing land supply in the first three quarters of this financial year is expected to support some 15 680 units, which has already exceeded our annual target of private housing supply, i.e. 12 600 units," Ms Linn said. Ms Linn continued, "Although the target has already been met, we will continue to roll out land to the market in the third quarter based on three considerations: (1) the annual supply target is not a rigid indicator, the Government has all along evaluated the pace and trend of market supply in its totality from a macro perspective; (2) some development projects co-ordinated by the Government (e.g. the Northern Metropolis, railway property development and urban renewal projects) have their own specific timeframes in meeting the Government's policy needs and the holistic development of their respective areas; and (3) with the generally positive market sentiment, there is sufficient demand and capacity for developers to take on mature urban land. The Government will continue to assess the circumstances and roll out land flexibly according to policy needs and market conditions." The site to be tendered from October to December 2026 is in the Annex. The actual tender timetable will be drawn up taking into account the progress of necessary preparatory work. The Lands Department will announce the detailed land sale arrangements before individual sites are put up for tender.

items.title: Enhancement works to commence in Central Government-Aided Emergency Hospital
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Hospital Authority: The Hospital Authority (HA) spokesperson announced today (October 15) that the Central Government-Aided Emergency Hospital (CGAEH) located in the Loop will undergo facilities enhancement works starting from October 20 (Tuesday), to provide patients with a better treatment environment. The works are expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027. Services at the CGAEH will be temporarily suspended during the works and will resume upon the completion of the project. The spokesperson said, "The CGAEH has been in operation for over three years since April 2023, and hospital facilities generally require maintenance works every two to three years. The HA will carry out enhancement works based on facility usage and service needs. The project covers replacing the ceiling insulation materials, reinforcing and repairing frequently used flooring, and conducting routine maintenance of air-conditioning systems to maintain the stable temperature and humidity control required for precision medical equipment. Supplementary water tanks will also be installed to enhance the resilience of the water supply system and maintain water supply during emergencies." The project aims to improve the hospital's environment and relevant facilities, making them better suited to daily operational requirements, providing patients with a more comfortable environment for examination and treatment, supporting healthcare workers in delivering services, and enhancing the patient experience. The works are scheduled to take place during the autumn and winter seasons to avoid the rainy season as much as possible, thereby minimising the impact of heavy rain and other adverse weather conditions on the progress. This will facilitate the completion of the works as planned, allowing the CGAEH to resume services at the earliest possible time. In view of the works, the CGAEH will make appropriate arrangements for patients to ensure continuity of care and follow-up services. Patients scheduled for diagnostic radiology services, including computed tomography scan, magnetic resonance imaging scan and ultrasound scan, will be arranged to receive follow-up services at hospitals within their respective clusters. The hospital will contact the patients concerned in due course regarding their new appointment dates and examination venues. For patients who have booked sleep study services, urgent cases will be arranged to undergo testing at hospitals within their respective clusters, while the remaining non-urgent cases will be scheduled for testing after the CGAEH resumes services. Patients concerned will be notified of the relevant arrangements. The CGAEH has also contacted patients with scheduled endoscopy and intravitreal injection appointments and made arrangements for their services. The HA will issue push notifications through the mobile application HA Go to keep patients informed of the latest service updates. Patients may also check their latest appointment details via the "My Appointments" function on HA Go. For enquiries, patients may contact the CGAEH during office hours (see table below). items.title: Scam alert related to banks
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) wishes to alert members of the public to the press releases issued by the banks listed below relating to fraudulent websites, internet banking login screens, phishing emails or other scams, which have been reported to the HKMA. Hyperlinks to the press releases are available on the HKMA website . Bank Type of Scam The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited Fraudulent mobile application (App) OCBC Bank (Hong Kong) Limited Fraudulent website and internet banking login screen The HKMA wishes to remind the public that banks will not send SMS or emails with embedded hyperlinks which direct them to the banks' websites to carry out transactions. They will not ask customers for sensitive information, such as login passwords or One-Time Password, by phone, email or SMS (including via embedded hyperlinks). Anyone who has provided his or her personal information, or who has conducted any financial transactions, through or in response to the scams concerned, should contact the relevant bank with the information provided in the corresponding press release, and report the matter to the Crime Wing Information Centre of the Hong Kong Police Force at 2860 5012.

items.title: Hong Kong Customs organises Customs YES Youth International Engagement Tour to Macao (with photos)
items.description: Hong Kong Customs organised the Customs YES Youth International Engagement Tour to Macao on October 11 and 12. A total of 20 Customs YES members visited Macao. Through visits to the platform for commercial and trade co-operation between China and Portuguese-speaking countries, historical and cultural heritage sites, and local customs enforcement facilities, members gained a comprehensive understanding of Macao's unique advantages and hub functions in the country's overall opening-up. Members also participated in the 36th World Customs Organization (WCO) Asia/Pacific (A/P) Regional Contact Points Meeting to deepen their knowledge of international customs co-operation and frontier enforcement developments. To strengthen interactive exchanges between the youth of Hong Kong and Macao, the delegation first participated in a Portuguese egg tart baking workshop alongside members of "Jovens Protectores do Original", the youth programme of Macao Customs, to experience Macao's distinctive culinary culture and to forge friendships. The delegation subsequently visited the Maritime Enforcement Department of the Macao Customs Service and toured its fleet to gain insights into Macao Customs' enforcement work in safeguarding maritime security, conducting marine patrols, and combating smuggling. To enhance members' understanding of Macao's strategic positioning as "One Centre, One Platform and One Base", the delegation visited the Pavilion of China-Portuguese-speaking Countries Commercial and Trade Service Platform to learn about the development of economic and trade co-operation between the country and Portuguese-speaking nations, as well as Macao's bridging role in fostering Sino-Portuguese economic, trade, and cultural exchanges and co-operation. As this year marks the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the delegation also visited General Ye Ting's Former Residence to learn about the heroic deeds of the revolutionary predecessor, and modern Chinese history, thereby fostering their affection for and sense of belonging to the country. In addition, members toured cultural landmarks including the Ruins of St. Paul's, the Mount Fortress, and Rua do Cunha, experiencing firsthand the profound cultural heritage blending Chinese and Western influences in Macao. Making full use of its capacity as the WCO Vice-Chair for the A/P region, Hong Kong Customs actively facilitated youth engagement on the global stage by specially arranging for the delegation to participate in the 36th WCO A/P Regional Contact Points Meeting held in Macao. During the welcoming reception of the meeting, Customs YES members assisted in receiving foreign guests and, for the first time, worked with a Macao youth representative to serve as masters of ceremonies. The youths from both sides demonstrated confidence and dedication in front of customs delegates across the Asia-Pacific region, telling the good stories of contemporary China and Hong Kong on the international stage. ​ Customs YES will continue to organise diversified Mainland and international exchange activities in alignment with the National 15th Five-Year Plan and the relevant policy directions set out in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan. These initiatives aim to help young people broaden their global horizons, enhance their understanding of the development positioning of both the country and Hong Kong, and encourage them to proactively equip themselves, leverage their strengths, and actively integrate into and serve the overall development of the nation.

items.title: Incoming passenger convicted and jailed for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes (with photo)
items.description: An incoming male passenger was sentenced to nine months' imprisonment and fined $2,000 by the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts today (October 15) for importing duty-not-paid cigarettes and failing to declare them to Customs officers, in contravention of the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (DCO). Customs officers intercepted an incoming 30-year-old Mainland male passenger arriving in Hong Kong from Phnom Penh, Cambodia, at Hong Kong International Airport yesterday (October 14) and seized about 82 400 duty-not-paid cigarettes, with an estimated market value of about $371,000 and a duty potential of about $273,000, from his personal baggage. The passenger was subsequently arrested. Customs welcomes the sentence. The custodial sentence has imposed a considerable deterrent effect and reflects the seriousness of the offences. Customs reminds members of the public that under the DCO, cigarettes are dutiable goods to which the DCO applies. Any person who imports, deals with, possesses, sells or buys duty-not-paid cigarettes commits an offence. The maximum penalty upon conviction is a fine of $2 million and imprisonment for seven years. Members of the public may report any suspected illicit cigarette activities to Customs' 24-hour hotline 182 8080 or its dedicated crime-reporting email account ( crimereport@customs.gov.hk ) or online form ( eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002 ).

items.title: Lands Department releases figures on registered lease modifications, land exchanges, private treaty grants and lot extensions in third quarter of 2026
items.description: The Lands Department (LandsD) announced today (October 15) that it registered 12 lease modifications, two land exchanges and one lot extension in the Land Registry during the quarter ending September 2026, of which two were modifications of a technical nature involving nil premium. Among these 15 land transactions, five are located on Hong Kong Island, seven are in Kowloon and three are in the New Territories. The transactions exclude Small House cases. A further seven lots were granted by private treaty during the period. One was granted to the Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park Company Limited wholly-owned by the Government for the development of an industry park; one was granted for the development of innovation and technology park and the talent accommodation in the Loop; one was granted for garden use in Shek O; one was granted to the MTR Corporation Limited for residential development in Yuen Long; one was granted to the Urban Renewal Authority for residential development in Hung Hom; and the other two were granted to the Hong Kong Housing Authority for public housing developments. The above land transactions realised a total land premium of about $2,934.347 million. Transaction records of the lease modifications, land exchanges, private treaty grants and lot extensions, including those registered recently, are uploaded to the LandsD website ( www.landsd.gov.hk/en/land-disposal-transaction/land-transaction.html ) on a monthly basis. Details of the transactions may be obtained by searching the registered documents in the Land Registry.

items.title: Government posts land resumption and acquisition notices for development of Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area (First Batch)
items.description: The Lands Department (LandsD) today (October 15) posted resumption notices in accordance with section 4 of the Lands Resumption Ordinance (Chapter 124) and acquisition notices in accordance with section 4 of the Land Acquisition (Possessory Title) Ordinance (Chapter 130) for the development of Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area (NTM NDA) (First Batch). The Government will resume 1 043 private lots with an area of about 62 hectares, and acquire the government land occupied by 23 graves and 22 urns of about 450 square metres, as well as the government land with 27 fishponds of about 2 700 sq m. The said land will revert to and vest in the Government upon the expiry of a period of three months from the date of affixing the notices (i.e. January 16, 2027). The abovementioned land reversion date and land vesting date are not the departure deadlines for the affected households and business undertakings. The LandsD will post notices in the relevant areas about three months before the applicable departure deadlines, requiring affected parties to depart in batches according to the project programme. It is now estimated that the affected households and business undertakings will have to move out in batches from the second quarter of 2027 at the earliest. The LandsD and its appointed Community Liaison Service Team will maintain close liaison with the affected parties to handle the compensation and rehousing matters. The NTM NDA is the fifth NDA development being commenced in the Northern Metropolis and will be developed in conjunction with the San Tin Technopole to establish the San Tin University Town based on the concept of town area. The campus area in the NTM NDA is about 52 hectares, including an area of about five hectares reserved for the construction of the third medical school. Site formation and infrastructure works for the NTM NDA is scheduled to commence in the first half of next year, and the "spade-ready sites" will be available progressively starting from the end of 2028.

items.title: Tender of 2-year RMB HKSAR Institutional Government Bonds through re-opening to be held on October 22
items.description: The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority: ​The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), as representative of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government (HKSAR Government), announced today (October 15) that a tender of 2-year RMB institutional Government Bonds (Bonds) through the re-opening of existing 3-year Government Bond issue 03GB2807001 under the Infrastructure Bond Programme will be held on October 22, 2026 (Thursday), for settlement on October 26, 2026 (Monday). An additional amount of RMB0.75 billion of the outstanding 3-year Bonds (issue no. 03GB2807001) will be on offer. The Bonds will mature on July 28, 2028 and will carry interest at the rate of 1.59 per cent per annum payable semi-annually in arrear. The Indicative Pricings of the Bonds on October 15, 2026 are 100.27 with a semi-annualised yield of 1.435 per cent. Tender is open only to Primary Dealers appointed under the Infrastructure Bond Programme. Anyone wishing to apply for the Bonds on offer can do so through any of the Primary Dealers on the latest published list, which can be obtained from the Hong Kong Government Bonds website at www.hkgb.gov.hk . Each tender must be for an amount of RMB50,000 or integral multiples thereof. Tender results will be published on the HKMA's website, the Hong Kong Government Bonds website, Bloomberg (GBHK ) and Refinitiv (IBPGSBPINDEX). The publication time is expected to be no later than 3pm on the tender day. HKSAR Institutional Government Bonds Tender Information Tender information of 2-year RMB HKSAR Institutional Government Bonds: Issue Number : 03GB2807001 Stock Code : 85039 (HKGB1.59 2807-R) Tender Date and Time : October 22, 2026 (Thursday) 9.30am to 10.30am Issue and Settlement Date : October 26, 2026 (Monday) Amount on Offer : RMB0.75 billion Maturity : 2 years Remaining Maturity : Approximately 1.76 years Maturity Date : July 28, 2028 (Friday) Interest Rate : 1.59 per cent p.a. payable semi-annually in arrear Interest Payment Dates : January 28 and July 28 in each year, commencing on the Issue Date up to and including the Maturity Date, subject to adjustment in accordance with the terms of the Institutional Issuances Information Memorandum of the Infrastructure Bond Programme and Government Sustainable Bond Programme (Information Memorandum) published on the Hong Kong Government Bonds website. Method of Tender : Competitive tender Tender Amount : Each competitive tender must be for an amount of RMB50,000 or integral multiples thereof. Any tender applications for the Bonds must be submitted through a Primary Dealer on the latest published list. The accrued interest to be paid by successful bidders on the issue date (October 26, 2026) for the tender amount is RMB196.03 per minimum denomination of RMB50,000. (The accrued interest to be paid for tender amount exceeding RMB50,000 may not be exactly equal to the figures calculated from the accrued interest per minimum denomination of RMB50,000 due to rounding). Other Details : Please see the Information Memorandum available on the Hong Kong Government Bonds website or approach Primary Dealers. Expected commencement date of dealing on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited : The tender amount is fully fungible with the existing 03GB2807001 (Stock code: 85039) listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong. Use of Proceeds : The Bonds will be issued under the institutional part of the Infrastructure Bond Programme. Proceeds will be invested in infrastructure projects in accordance with the Infrastructure Bond Framework published on the Hong Kong Government Bonds website.
